name: Universal (applies to every deal)
summary: Chapter 0 of The Bible on Due Diligence v2, as a request library merged into every deal-type packet. It covers what applies regardless of asset class: sponsor and principal identity, background, track record and leadership; KYC, AML, sanctions, source of funds and source of wealth; fraud controls (segregation of duties, independent administrator, custodian and auditor, proof of cash, direct third-party confirmation); verification of funds, assets, title and every claim on the same asset; the valuation model and its base, downside, flat-margin and exit-multiple cases; counterparty, treasury and liquidity risk; the credit-cycle overlay; compliance and misconduct; insurance, physical-climate, water and policy risk; preservation of legal remedies; and the November 2026 regulatory status lines. The spine: verify the sponsor, verify the cash, verify the collateral or the earnings, verify the legal title, verify that you see every claim on the same asset, and separate what you confirmed from what you could not.
one_check: Get it from the third party, not from the sponsor: segregation of duties plus direct, unsolicited confirmation of cash, custody, wire authority and every claim on the same collateral (bank confirmations, the administrator's wire matrix, the custodian's statement, the processor's revenue file, a UCC sweep across all affiliates).

subtypes.name: Operating company
subtypes.description: The deal underwrites an operating business with revenue, EBITDA, employees and customers (buyout, growth, venture, business debt, roll-up).

subtypes.name: Fund or adviser sponsor
subtypes.description: The sponsor is a GP, registered or exempt reporting adviser, or the investment is a pooled vehicle (fund, co-invest, SPV, continuation vehicle).

subtypes.name: Private placement to investors
subtypes.description: The sponsor raises money from investors under Reg D (506(b) or 506(c)) or a similar private offering.

subtypes.name: Long-lived real asset
subtypes.description: Real estate, infrastructure, energy, agriculture, data centers or other long-lived physical assets exposed to climate, water, grid and insurability risk.

subtypes.name: Levered vehicle or financing lines
subtypes.description: The target, fund or co-investor uses warehouse, repo, margin, subscription, NAV, asset-based or other short-term secured financing, or total-return swaps.

subtypes.name: Loan book, receivables or stated-income pool
subtypes.description: Returns or collateral come from loans, receivables, leases or borrower- or tenant-stated income.

subtypes.name: Crypto exposure
subtypes.description: Any investor, principal or counterparty with crypto-derived wealth; crypto custody, exchanges or lenders; stablecoins or tokenized cash held as treasury or collateral.

subtypes.name: Government or policy dependent
subtypes.description: Cash flow depends on a government lease, appropriation, tax credit, green bank, ratepayer charge, concession or regulated tariff.

subtypes.name: Public filer
subtypes.description: Public target, take-private, carve-out from a public parent, or public borrower with periodic SEC filings.

subtypes.name: Acquisition under a purchase agreement
subtypes.description: Control or minority acquisition documented with reps, indemnities, R&W insurance or an MAE clause.

subtypes.name: Earnout
subtypes.description: Any part of the consideration is contingent on post-closing milestones.

subtypes.name: Stock as consideration
subtypes.description: We or the seller receive the counterparty's stock (including de-SPAC) as consideration.

subtypes.name: Venture or structured equity security
subtypes.description: A priced round, SAFE, convertible or structured equity with liquidation preferences, ratchets or participation, or marks set by a prior round.

subtypes.name: Semi-liquid or evergreen vehicle
subtypes.description: Interval fund, non-traded BDC, NAV REIT, tender-offer or evergreen fund with periodic redemptions and gates.

subtypes.name: Consumer-demand exposure
subtypes.description: Consumer credit, consumer brands, housing or any deal whose exit depends on consumer demand.

subtypes.name: Subscription or repeat-purchase business
subtypes.description: SaaS, DTC, marketplaces or consumer subscription where value is driven by cohorts.

subtypes.name: Franchise, multi-unit, staffing or roll-up
subtypes.description: Labor-market antitrust exposure through franchise, employment or vendor agreements.

subtypes.name: Health care or government contractor
subtypes.description: Revenue from government payors or government contracts, with False Claims Act and kickback exposure.

subtypes.name: Regulated manufacturing
subtypes.description: Pharma, food, supplements or medical devices subject to FDA quality and data-integrity rules.

subtypes.name: Foreign agents, government customers or currency mismatch
subtypes.description: Foreign sales agents, foreign government customers or licences, international counterparties, or revenue and debt in different currencies or pegs.

subtypes.name: Material hedges or derivatives
subtypes.description: The borrower, fund or co-investor carries material swaps, options or other derivatives.

subtypes.name: Bank-like counterparty or regional lender
subtypes.description: A bank, credit union, fintech or specialty lender funded by deposits or short-term money is the borrower, lender, or holds the construction, bridge or revolving commitment.

subtypes.name: Insurer or permanent-capital counterparty
subtypes.description: The lender, LP or counterparty is an insurer, or a manager whose permanent capital is an affiliated insurer.

intake_questions.question: In one line: what is the deal, and what are you asking our syndicate for?
intake_questions.why: Universal deck order item 1 (0.8); a sponsor who cannot state the asset and the ask in one line is not ready for diligence.

intake_questions.question: Which deal type is it? Choose one or more of: real-estate, business-debt, credit, tech-venture, pe-ma, cpg-consumer, cannabis-hemp, growth-equity, energy-infrastructure, data-centers, crypto-digital-assets, niche-assets, fund, secondaries, nav-lending, evergreen, search-fund, healthcare, litigation-finance.
intake_questions.why: Selects which deal-type library is merged with the universal list; hybrids get every matching library.

intake_questions.question: What is the asset class and the specific asset or business (sector, geography, stage: pre-revenue, growth, stabilized, distressed, construction)?
intake_questions.why: Drives depth of each workstream and which universal conditions apply (0.1, 0.6).

intake_questions.question: What is the total raise and our proposed allocation, the minimum ticket, and the total capitalization (sources and uses)?
intake_questions.why: Sizes the diligence floor and the 506(c) minimum-investment route ($200,000 natural persons, $1,000,000 entities) (0.3, 0.18).

intake_questions.question: What instrument are we being offered: common or preferred equity, LP interest, SAFE or convertible, senior or junior debt, revenue share, token, or other? Any liquidation preferences, ratchets or participation?
intake_questions.why: Value the specific security, not the headline post-money (0.6); sets venture-security and credit conditions.

intake_questions.question: Is this a control acquisition, minority investment, loan, fund commitment, co-investment or secondary? Is there a purchase agreement with reps, an earnout or stock consideration?
intake_questions.why: Sets m-and-a, earnout and stock-consideration conditions and the remedies workstream (0.16).

intake_questions.question: What is the use of proceeds, line by line, and how much goes to the sponsor or affiliates (fees, repayment of sponsor loans, buyouts of insiders)?
intake_questions.why: IC memo item 2 (0.7); insider steering and fee leakage are classic sales-side tells (0.4).

intake_questions.question: What is the timeline to commitment, funding and close, and is there any deadline imposed by the seller or another investor?
intake_questions.why: A seller-imposed deadline is a red flag, not a reason to cut the diligence floor (0.1).

intake_questions.question: Who is the sponsor: legal entity, principals, control persons, and who will release wires? Is the sponsor a registered or exempt reporting investment adviser (CRD/IAPD number)?
intake_questions.why: Starts identity, background and Form ADV work (0.2, 0.3); sets the fund-manager condition.

intake_questions.question: Who else is investing, in what amounts, and is there a lead investor? What diligence has the lead done (hours with management in person, sites visited, references called), and may we contact them directly?
intake_questions.why: Social proof is not diligence (0.4, 0.12); a lead that cannot state its diligence intensity is a red flag (0.1).

intake_questions.question: Is the sponsor or lead investing its own capital, how much, and is its main fund taking its full pro rata? Why is the deal being syndicated?
intake_questions.why: Co-investments underperform the main fund on average; ask why the GP is syndicating (0.13).

intake_questions.question: How was the deal sourced? Is it claimed to be proprietary, who else saw it, and did a banker or broker run a process?
intake_questions.why: A proprietary claim is an assertion to verify (0.1).

intake_questions.question: Which jurisdictions are involved: where are the sponsor, the issuer, the assets, the investors, the customers and the banks? Any foreign sales agents, government customers, or revenue and debt in different currencies?
intake_questions.why: Drives sanctions lists (UN, EU, UK), FCPA diligence and currency-mismatch tests (0.3, 0.11, 0.15); sets foreign-exposure.

intake_questions.question: Is the offering made under Rule 506(b), 506(c) or another exemption, and how are investors verified as accredited investors or qualified purchasers?
intake_questions.why: 506(c) requires documentary verification, not self-certification (0.3); sets private-offering.

intake_questions.question: Does the deal, the vehicle or any principal or counterparty involve crypto assets, crypto-derived wealth, stablecoins or tokenized cash?
intake_questions.why: Triggers address-level OFAC screening, on-chain tracing and key-control checks (0.3, 0.4); sets crypto-exposure.

intake_questions.question: Does the target or vehicle use leverage: subscription line, NAV facility, warehouse, repo, margin, asset-based, factoring, supply-chain finance or total-return swaps? Any material hedges?
intake_questions.why: Advance rates and haircuts are state variables; off-balance-sheet financing must be added to leverage (0.4, 0.10, 0.11); sets levered-vehicle and hedged.

intake_questions.question: Do returns come from a loan book, receivables, leases, or borrower- or tenant-stated income?
intake_questions.why: Sets credit-pool: loan-level dedupe, IRS-transcript income verification, static-pool tests (0.4, 0.5, 0.10).

intake_questions.question: Is the vehicle semi-liquid or evergreen (periodic redemptions, gates, tender offers)?
intake_questions.why: Liquidity coverage and gate tests (0.11); sets semi-liquid.

intake_questions.question: Does any revenue depend on a government lease, appropriation, tax credit (45Y, 48E, 45X), green bank, ratepayer charge, concession or regulated tariff?
intake_questions.why: The government decision is a counterparty (0.20); sets government-dependent.

intake_questions.question: Is the asset a long-lived physical asset (real estate, infrastructure, energy, agriculture, data center), and where exactly is it located?
intake_questions.why: Triggers insurability, water and grid-event screens (0.19); sets real-asset.

intake_questions.question: Is the target public, a take-private, a carve-out from a public parent, or a public borrower?
intake_questions.why: Triggers the 8-quarter filing diff (Lazy Prices) (0.4); sets public-filer.

intake_questions.question: Is the target in health care, government contracting, pharma, food, supplements, medical devices, franchising, staffing or a multi-unit roll-up?
intake_questions.why: Triggers False Claims Act, data-integrity and labor-antitrust diligence (0.15); sets healthcare-govcontract, regulated-manufacturing, franchise-multiunit.

intake_questions.question: Is the business subscription or repeat-purchase, and does the exit depend on consumer demand?
intake_questions.why: Triggers cohort (CBCV) diligence and the household-debt downside case (0.6, 0.10); sets subscription-repeat and consumer-exposed.

intake_questions.question: Is any lender, LP or key counterparty a bank, regional lender, specialty finance company, or insurer (or an insurer-affiliated manager)?
intake_questions.why: Triggers bank-like counterparty and insurer statutory-capital tests (0.11); sets bank-like-counterparty and insurer-counterparty.

intake_questions.question: What return are you projecting (gross and net IRR, MOIC, yield), over what hold, and what base rate must this beat?
intake_questions.why: A memo that does not state the base rate cannot explain why the deal beats it (0.7); 20%+ net IRR for a generic strategy needs specific evidence (0.6).

intake_questions.question: Is there any pending or past litigation, regulatory inquiry, bankruptcy, or criminal matter involving the sponsor, any principal or the target?
intake_questions.why: Self-disclosure baseline to reconcile against the independent background check; 21% of managers misrepresented past problems (0.2).

requests.request: One-page summary stating what the deal is and the ask in one line: amount, instrument, our allocation, use of proceeds, structure and security.
requests.format: Sponsor-written one-pager or deck page 1, dated.
requests.why: A deal that cannot be stated in one line usually hides its structure (0.8 deck order item 1).
requests.pass: Amount, instrument, allocation, use of proceeds and security are each stated and tie to the sources-and-uses table to the dollar.
requests.fail: Ask, instrument or security missing or inconsistent with the model or term sheet.
requests.verify: Tie every figure to the sources-and-uses table and the draft term sheet.

requests.request: Investor deck in the universal order (ask, problem, asset, sponsor and track record, market and cycle, numbers, structure, returns with sensitivities, risks, terms), with every sponsor claim marked verified (and by whom) or asserted.
requests.format: PDF deck plus an editable claims register listing each factual claim, its source document and its verifier.
requests.why: Claims presented as fact that nobody independently sourced; investment cases resting on pitch delivery rather than evidence (0.12).
requests.pass: Every factual claim appears in the claims register with a source document; every 'verified' claim names a third party we can contact.
requests.fail: Claims with no source; 'verified' claims with no named verifier; deck cites round price, a marquee co-investor or a national forecast as validation.
requests.verify: Score the written materials and data room before the live pitch with a fixed rubric and more than one rater; contact each named verifier.

requests.request: Sources-and-uses table showing every dollar in and out, including all fees, reimbursements and payments to the sponsor, its affiliates or insiders.
requests.format: Excel, tied to the model and the draft closing funds flow.
requests.why: Insider steering and fee leakage hidden in use of proceeds (0.4 sales-side tells).
requests.pass: Sources equal uses; every payment to the sponsor, an affiliate or an insider is itemized and disclosed.
requests.fail: Unitemized 'other' or 'working capital' buckets; undisclosed payments to related parties; repayment of sponsor loans not disclosed.
requests.verify: Reconcile to the funds-flow memo at closing and to bank statements after funding.

requests.request: Live financial model (native Excel, formulas intact) with historicals, a base case and a downside case, and all assumptions on one input tab.
requests.format: Native .xlsx with no hard-coded outputs; version-dated.
requests.why: Returns that exist only as a PDF output cannot be stress tested (0.6, 0.7 item 5).
requests.pass: Model runs, ties to the historical financials, and contains a separately built downside case; no hard-coded outputs.
requests.fail: PDF-only model, hard-coded returns, or downside case that is the base case with a small haircut.
requests.verify: Rebuild the key outputs ourselves from the input tab; reconcile historicals to bank statements in the QoE.

requests.request: Historical financial statements for the last 3 fiscal years and year-to-date (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow), audited where audits exist.
requests.format: Auditor-signed statements where audited; otherwise accountant-reviewed or management statements clearly labelled.
requests.why: Projections with no verified history; sloppy numbers signal broader governance problems (0.2, 0.8).
requests.pass: Statements for every period are provided, internally consistent, and labelled audited, reviewed or management-prepared.
requests.fail: Missing periods, unexplained restatements, or adjusted figures with no GAAP reconciliation.
requests.verify: Obtain audited statements directly from the auditor with signed authorization; proof of cash in the QoE.

requests.request: Government-issued photo ID and proof of residential address for every principal, control person, director, CFO, controller and wire signatory of the sponsor and the issuer.
requests.format: Unexpired passport or driver's licence (color copy) plus a utility bill or bank statement under 90 days old; verified by live video or in person.
requests.why: Identity fraud, nominee principals and AI-generated identities (0.2, 0.3, 0.4).
requests.pass: Every named person has a valid, unexpired ID whose name and date of birth match the background-check report and the entity records.
requests.fail: Expired or inconsistent IDs, refusal to produce ID for a control person or wire releaser, or names that do not match entity filings.
requests.verify: Run document-authenticity checks through the background-check vendor and confirm identity on a live call initiated by us.

requests.request: Formation documents for the sponsor and every entity in the deal chain: certificate of formation or incorporation, operating agreement or bylaws, all amendments, and current good-standing certificates.
requests.format: Secretary-of-state certified copies; good-standing certificates dated within 30 days.
requests.why: Sham or lapsed entities and undisclosed control rights (0.2, 0.3).
requests.pass: Every entity exists, is in good standing, and its governing documents name the same managers and members as the org chart.
requests.fail: Entity not found, administratively dissolved, or governing documents naming persons absent from the org chart.
requests.verify: Pull each entity record ourselves from the secretary of state of each jurisdiction.

requests.request: Certified ownership and organization chart from each ultimate natural-person owner down to the deal vehicle, including every affiliate, principal-owned entity, SPV, JV and side vehicle.
requests.format: Chart certified by an officer, with percentage ownership and voting control on every link.
requests.why: Hidden affiliates hold assets, debts and pledges the lender never sees (First Brands, 0.4); no federal BOI registry to rely on (0.3, 0.18).
requests.pass: Chart reconciles to formation documents, cap tables and operating agreements; every entity on UCC and litigation searches appears on the chart.
requests.fail: Entities found in searches that are missing from the chart; circular or nominee ownership; refusal to certify.
requests.verify: Reconcile to state filings, UCC search debtor names and our own CDD; there is no federal BOI record for US companies after Aug. 14, 2026.

requests.request: Beneficial-ownership certification identifying every natural person who owns 25% or more of each entity in the chain, plus at least one control person, with ID for each.
requests.format: Signed certification in the form of the FinCEN CDD Rule (31 CFR 1010.230), supported by operating agreements and cap tables.
requests.why: Concealed owners, sanctioned owners and nominee structures (0.3).
requests.pass: Every 25%+ owner and a control person are named, identified and screened; ownership percentages tie to governing documents.
requests.fail: Unidentified owners, bearer shares, trusts with undisclosed beneficiaries, or ownership that does not tie.
requests.verify: Establish beneficial ownership through our own CDD (operating agreements, cap tables, certified charts); do not rely on CTA BOI filings, which US companies no longer make.

requests.request: Detailed resume for each principal and senior team member: every employer, title, dates, degrees, licences (Series, CPA, bar), and board seats for the last 20 years.
requests.format: Signed CV with month-level dates and contactable references for each role.
requests.why: Resume inflation is a documented fraud precursor (Drive Planning, Toltec Capital, 0.2).
requests.pass: Every employer, title, date, degree and licence is confirmed by the background-check firm or the issuing body.
requests.fail: Any unverifiable or inflated title, degree, licence or date range.
requests.verify: Background-check firm verifies employment and education directly; licences checked on FINRA BrokerCheck, IAPD and state boards.

requests.request: Signed self-disclosure questionnaire for the sponsor and each principal covering criminal matters, civil litigation, bankruptcies, judgments, liens, regulatory actions (SEC, FINRA, state), terminations and investigations in the last 10 years.
requests.format: Signed and dated questionnaire under penalty of rescission, with supporting documents for each disclosed item.
requests.why: 21% of managers misrepresented past legal or regulatory problems; 10% would have passed as clean on self-disclosure alone (0.2).
requests.pass: Every matter found by the independent background check was disclosed in the questionnaire.
requests.fail: Any material matter found independently that was not disclosed, or a partial disclosure ('strategic misstatement').
requests.verify: Reconcile item by item to the independent background check and Form ADV; record any refused question as a tracked field.

requests.request: Track-record summary listing every deal, fund and vehicle the sponsor and each principal has ever managed or led, including closed, abandoned and written-off ones, with amount invested, dates, realized and unrealized value, gross and net returns.
requests.format: Excel schedule, one row per deal or vehicle, with the principal who led each.
requests.why: Cherry-picked records, survivorship and backfill bias (0.13).
requests.pass: Schedule is complete: it reconciles to Form ADV, prior offering documents, public filings and references; no vehicle we find elsewhere is missing.
requests.fail: Omitted vehicles, returns shown only gross, compounded IRRs, or a record borrowed from people not primarily responsible.
requests.verify: Cross-check against Form ADV, SEC filings, press, prior LP references and state records; recompute from cash flows at confirmatory stage.

requests.request: Statement of the sponsor's deal pace and capacity: deals per year and AUM for each of the last 5 years against investment and operating headcount, and the annual deployment target against the size of the market it invests in.
requests.format: Table by year with headcount by function.
requests.why: Rapid growth in deal volume without the operating bench is associated with worse outcomes; deployment pressure undermines selective underwriting (0.2, 0.10).
requests.pass: Team size grew in step with deal pace and AUM; deployment target is a small share of the target market.
requests.fail: Deal pace or AUM doubling without a matching increase in senior team; deployment target a large share of the market.
requests.verify: Check headcount against LinkedIn and Form ADV Part 1 employee counts; deal counts against public records.

requests.request: Deal-sourcing statement: how the deal came to the sponsor, whether it is claimed to be proprietary, who else saw it, and whether a banker or broker ran a process.
requests.format: Written statement naming the intermediary, if any, and the other bidders or investors approached.
requests.why: Unverified 'proprietary deal' claims; a sponsor that claims to close far more than about 6 of 100 opportunities is not screening (0.1).
requests.pass: Claim corroborated by the intermediary or seller; sponsor's stated close rate is consistent with institutional funnels.
requests.fail: 'Proprietary' claim no one can corroborate; implausibly high close rate.
requests.verify: Ask the seller, banker or broker directly who else saw the deal.

requests.request: List of every other investor, lender and co-investor in the deal and the lead investor, with amounts, and written consent for us to contact each about the diligence it performed.
requests.format: Table with contact names; consent letter.
requests.why: Social proof substitutes for diligence ('X and Y are already in') (0.4, 0.12).
requests.pass: We confirm directly with each named investor that it is in and what diligence it performed.
requests.fail: Named investors who deny or downplay involvement, or sponsor refuses consent to contact.
requests.verify: Call each investor on an independently obtained number.

requests.request: Lead investor's diligence-intensity record: hours spent with management in person, sites visited, reference calls made, and what was skipped for timing.
requests.format: Written statement from the lead (not the sponsor), with dates.
requests.why: Diligence thins in hot markets and widens the spread of outcomes (Fu and Taylor, 0.1); VC norm is about 118 hours and about 10 reference calls per deal.
requests.pass: Lead states hours, sites and references; reference calls at or above about 10 (13 late-stage, 8 early-stage).
requests.fail: Lead cannot state hours, sites and references, or relies on another investor's work.
requests.verify: Confirm with the lead directly; record in our diligence-intensity field.

requests.request: Market and cycle statement: where the asset class is in the credit cycle, who bought recent comparables and how they were financed, new supply coming (issuance, construction, unlocks, queued capacity), and recent thematic vehicle launches in the same theme.
requests.format: Written memo with data sources (comps list with buyer type and financing source; supply pipeline).
requests.why: Cheap credit lets a small levered minority set prices; diligence thins at the top (0.10).
requests.pass: Statement addresses each line of the 0.10 cycle scorecard with sources; if 3 or more bubble features are present, it names the exit buyer and multiple once supply arrives.
requests.fail: Deck cites the round's price, a marquee co-investor or a national demand forecast as validation in an asset class scoring late-cycle on 3 or more lines.
requests.verify: We score the 0.10 scorecard ourselves from BIS, Fed Z.1, REIT-implied caps, fund-launch counts and the comps' financing.

requests.request: Statement of every law, regulation, exemption, licence, tax credit or agency decision the deal relies on, with its current status and the sponsor's description of it.
requests.format: Written schedule with citations, reviewed by sponsor counsel.
requests.why: Decks describe rules that have changed (for example 'cannabis is now Schedule III' is wrong for adult-use) (0.18, A.3 item 29).
requests.pass: Each line is current as of November 2026 per the 0.18 status table and will be re-checked at signing.
requests.fail: Any reliance on a vacated, postponed or misdescribed rule (SEC Private Fund Adviser rules, IA AML rule, CTA BOI, 506(c) relief, cannabis scheduling, IRA credits).
requests.verify: Our counsel checks each line against the primary source at signing.

requests.request: Form ADV Parts 1 and 2 (and 2B brochure supplements), the adviser's CRD and IAPD numbers, and the sponsor's completed DDQ (ILPA DDQ 2.0 format preferred).
requests.format: Current filings as on IAPD; DDQ signed by the CCO.
requests.why: Past legal and regulatory problems in Form ADV relate to conflicts, concentration and leverage; DDQ answers diverge from filings (0.2).
requests.pass: Every Form ADV disclosure item reconciles to the DDQ and self-disclosure answers.
requests.fail: Unreconciled disclosure items; adviser not registered or exempt-reporting when it should be; DDQ questions refused.
requests.verify: Pull Form ADV ourselves from IAPD; where no ADV exists, estimate operational risk from public data (omega score, WEAK).

requests.request: Plain-language glossary: every term of art in the deck and model ('adjusted EBITDA', 'synthetic', 'visibility', 'hedge', 'compute', 'distribution rate') restated in one sentence with a number attached.
requests.format: Written glossary annex.
requests.why: Opaque jargon lets committees approve what they do not understand (London Whale, 0.12).
requests.pass: Every key term is restated in one plain sentence with a number that ties to the model.
requests.fail: Any key term the sponsor cannot restate with a number.
requests.verify: IC members test each definition against the model; items no one in the approval chain can restate are not approved.

requests.request: Timeline to signing, funding and close, with any deadline imposed by the seller, the lead or another investor and the reason for it.
requests.format: Written timeline.
requests.why: Seller-imposed deadlines are used to cut the diligence floor (0.1).
requests.pass: Timeline accommodates the full diligence floor (site visits, in-person management hours, reference calls, third-party reports).
requests.fail: Deadline that leaves no time for third-party reports or direct confirmations; pressure to act fast.
requests.verify: We set the diligence floor in writing before the timeline is agreed and do not shrink it for competition.

requests.request: Draft term sheet or LOI with economics, security, conditions precedent, information and audit rights, consent rights, and exclusivity period.
requests.format: Marked draft in Word.
requests.why: Rights not negotiated before signing are not available later; LPs and minority investors rarely win in court (0.16).
requests.pass: Term sheet includes information rights, audited financials, inspection and audit rights, and conditions precedent tied to the gating items in this packet.
requests.fail: No information or audit rights; no conditions precedent for third-party reports; exclusivity without diligence access.
requests.verify: Our counsel marks up against the gating items list.

requests.request: Signed consent and authorization for independent background checks (criminal, civil, bankruptcy, regulatory, credit, media) on the sponsor, every principal, the CFO, controller, wire releaser and every placement agent or salesperson.
requests.format: FCRA-compliant consent forms signed by each individual.
requests.why: Fraud is usually collusive; second-tier executives and sales agents are defendants in placement frauds (Drive Planning, 0.2).
requests.pass: Consents received for every named person in the chain, including the placement chain.
requests.fail: Any principal, finance officer, wire releaser or placement agent refuses consent.
requests.verify: Background-check firm confirms receipt and validity of every consent.

requests.request: Signed authorization letters allowing us and our QoE provider to obtain statements and confirmations directly and unsolicited from every bank, custodian, administrator, auditor, prime broker, servicer and payment processor.
requests.format: Signed letters addressed to each institution, on its own form where required.
requests.why: Statements produced by the manager rather than a third party are the Ponzi enabler (0.4, 0.5).
requests.pass: Authorization covers every institution that holds cash, assets or records for the sponsor and the deal.
requests.fail: Refusal to authorize direct contact with any administrator, auditor, custodian, prime broker or bank.
requests.verify: Send requests ourselves to contact details obtained independently, not from the sponsor.

requests.request: Fully diluted capitalization table (all classes, options, RSUs, warrants, SAFEs, convertibles, benefit-fund issuance) and a list of every investor veto or consent right over financings and M&A.
requests.format: Excel cap table reconciled to the stock ledger and charter; schedule of veto rights with document references.
requests.why: Headline valuations use basic share counts; strategic investors with financing vetoes block rescue capital (0.6, 0.16).
requests.pass: Cap table ties to the stock ledger, charter and option plan; price per share uses the fully diluted count; vetoes listed.
requests.fail: Unreconciled cap table; omitted SAFEs or warrants; undisclosed strategic investor financing veto.
requests.verify: Reconcile to charter filings, board minutes and transfer-agent or ledger records.

requests.request: Statement of the sponsor's own capital at risk in this deal, the main fund's participation and pro rata, and why the deal is being syndicated to us.
requests.format: Written statement with commitment amounts and source of the sponsor's cash.
requests.why: Co-investments and side vehicles underperform the sponsoring GP's main fund on average (adverse selection) (0.13).
requests.pass: Main fund takes its full pro rata and the sponsor has material capital at risk on the same terms as us.
requests.fail: Main fund under-allocates, sponsor has no money at risk, or syndication exists to offload a deal the main fund will not hold.
requests.verify: Confirm the main fund's allocation from the fund's administrator or capital-call notices.

requests.request: Schedule of every fee, expense reimbursement and economic interest the sponsor and affiliates will receive (acquisition, asset management, monitoring, transaction, director, financing, disposition fees, carry or promote), and how fees offset.
requests.format: Fee schedule with formulas and illustrative dollar amounts at base and downside cases.
requests.why: Fee overcharging and missed offsets are recurring SEC findings (TZP Management, 0.15).
requests.pass: All fees disclosed with formulas; offsets computed; sponsor economics reconcile to the model.
requests.fail: Undisclosed fees, fees on committed rather than invested capital after the investment period, or no offset of portfolio-company fees.
requests.verify: Recompute fee offsets from portfolio-company payments.

requests.request: Distribution policy and any stated distribution rate or yield, with the cash source of each projected distribution.
requests.format: Written policy and model tab mapping each distribution to an operating cash flow line.
requests.why: A fixed distribution rate on an illiquid asset paid from new capital is the Ponzi signature (GPB Capital, Heller ATMs, 0.4).
requests.pass: Every projected distribution is funded from asset-level operating cash flow in the model; no fixed or guaranteed rate.
requests.fail: Guaranteed or fixed above-market returns; distributions funded by new capital, borrowing or return of capital described as yield.
requests.verify: After funding, reconcile every distribution to its source account (monitoring item).

requests.request: Proposed information and reporting package: quarterly financial statements and fee and performance statements, annual audit by a named auditor, valuation reports, covenant certificates, and notice obligations.
requests.format: Draft reporting covenant or side-letter language; ILPA Reporting Template for funds.
requests.why: No federal rule requires quarterly statements, fund audits or GP-led fairness opinions since the SEC Private Fund Adviser rules were vacated on June 5, 2024 (0.16, 0.18).
requests.pass: Quarterly statements, an annual audit by a named auditor, and notice of material events are contractual obligations with fixed delivery deadlines.
requests.fail: Reporting left to sponsor discretion; no audit requirement; no fee and expense disclosure.
requests.verify: Our counsel confirms the obligations are in the operative documents, not only in the deck.

requests.request: Proposed fund governance terms: LPAC composition and consent rights (conflicts, GP-leds, NAV loans, extensions), key-person provisions with dissolution or suspension, for-cause removal standard and no-fault removal threshold.
requests.format: LPA draft sections or term summary.
requests.why: LPs rarely sue (4% of suits against top and bottom 50 PE firms); the protection is what you negotiate before signing (0.16).
requests.pass: Key-person dissolution or suspension and a workable removal right both exist; LPAC must consent to conflicted transactions, GP-leds and NAV debt.
requests.fail: Neither key-person dissolution nor a workable removal right: treat as no governance.
requests.verify: Our counsel reviews the LPA and side letter.

requests.request: Organization chart of the sponsor and target finance and operations functions naming the CFO, controller, the person who releases wires, the person who reconciles accounts, and the person who reports to investors.
requests.format: Chart with names, titles, reporting lines and tenure.
requests.why: One person deciding, moving cash and reporting is the most consistent precursor to fraud; a 'CFO' who is really a controller is a gap (0.2, 0.4).
requests.pass: Decision, cash movement and reporting sit with different people and an independent third party; titles match the work done.
requests.fail: Same person decides, releases wires and reports; no CFO able to give an independent view; long-tenured closed inner circle controlling reporting and cash.
requests.verify: Compare with the bank or administrator signatory list and with interviews of staff below the principals.

requests.request: Sponsor's walk-away price or maximum leverage and the conservative cash-flow case it is based on, set before bidding.
requests.format: Written note with the conservative case attached.
requests.why: Diligence run to confirm an answer already chosen is the most common M&A process failure (0.1, 0.12).
requests.pass: Walk-away price is set from conservative cash flows by people separate from the deal champions.
requests.fail: No walk-away price, or the deal champion also runs the valuation.
requests.verify: Our own valuation team sets our walk-away independently of the deal team.

requests.request: Track record as dated LP-level (or deal-level) cash flows for every fund, vehicle and deal ever managed, including closed and abandoned ones, so we can recompute returns ourselves.
requests.format: Excel cash-flow ledger (dates, contributions, distributions, residual NAV) tied to capital-account statements from the administrator.
requests.why: A track record is the sponsor's own exhibit; compounded IRRs, gross-only and selective periods are SEC exam findings (0.13).
requests.pass: We recompute gross and net IRR, TVPI, DPI and a PME (KS-PME) from the cash flows and they match the sponsor's reported figures, with every difference explained in writing; shown with and without the top 1 or 2 outcomes.
requests.fail: Returns we cannot recompute; IRRs compounded or compared with a time-weighted index; record collapses without the top 1 or 2 outcomes in a 'consistent singles' thesis.
requests.verify: Obtain capital-account statements from the administrator directly and confirm with two or more prior LPs.

requests.request: ILPA Performance Template (2025) for every prior fund, showing gross and net IRR and TVPI with and without the subscription facility and NAV debt, and subscription-line interest as a separate expense line.
requests.format: ILPA template in native format, one per fund, reconciled to audited financials.
requests.why: Subscription lines and NAV loans inflate interim IRR and DPI near a fundraise (0.13).
requests.pass: Template provided for every prior fund; returns with and without fund leverage both shown; facility use within ILPA reference points (15% to 25% of commitments, 180 days outstanding).
requests.fail: Refusal to provide the template (a signal in itself); facility above reference points; NAV debt used to fund distributions before a raise.
requests.verify: Tie to audited fund financials and facility agreements; ask the lender for drawn balances by date.

requests.request: Deal-by-deal attribution: for each realized deal, the partners who sourced, led and managed it, whether each is still with the sponsor and in what role.
requests.format: Table per deal with names and current status.
requests.why: Reputation and skill sit with partners; records borrowed from people who have left are an SEC finding (0.13).
requests.pass: Partners responsible for the majority of realized value are still at the sponsor and will lead this deal.
requests.fail: Track record attributed to departed people, or this deal led by someone with no record.
requests.verify: Confirm with references, former partners and LinkedIn histories.

requests.request: Return decomposition for every realized deal: revenue and EBITDA growth, debt paydown and leverage, multiple change, and dividend recaps, as separate lines.
requests.format: Excel bridge per deal from entry to exit equity value.
requests.why: Returns from multiple expansion and financial engineering are not repeatable (0.7 item 6, 0.13).
requests.pass: Operating improvement (earnings growth) explains the majority of realized value creation across the record.
requests.fail: Record driven mainly by multiple expansion, leverage or recaps; decomposition refused.
requests.verify: Recompute from entry and exit financials and purchase prices in deal documents.

requests.request: Monthly (or quarterly) return series for every strategy and vehicle, with drawdowns, leverage, and any option-like or short-volatility exposure described.
requests.format: Excel return series from the administrator, net and gross.
requests.why: Sharpe, Sortino and alpha can be manufactured; smooth returns are the Ponzi tell; short-vol looks like alpha (0.13).
requests.pass: Volatility and drawdowns are consistent with the stated strategy and asset class; a manipulation-proof measure (MPPM) and a levered put-writing benchmark do not erase the claimed alpha.
requests.fail: Returns smooth relative to strategy; Sharpe or Sortino offered as proof of skill for an options or leverage strategy; alpha indistinguishable from index put-writing.
requests.verify: Compute MPPM ourselves; compare with a levered index put-writing series where the strategy has crash exposure.

requests.request: Benchmark statement for every peer comparison or 'top quartile' claim: the benchmark name, vintage, whether it excludes backfill and includes dead funds, and the risk-matched public alternative (PME against a levered small-value index for buyouts).
requests.format: Written note with data source and extraction date.
requests.why: Backfill and survivorship bias inflate peer averages by several hundred bp (0.13).
requests.pass: Benchmark is named, vintage-matched, survivor-inclusive and risk-matched; net alpha is positive against it.
requests.fail: 'Top quartile' without naming the benchmark, vintage and dead-fund treatment.
requests.verify: Pull the benchmark ourselves; haircut unadjusted peer averages by several hundred bp.

requests.request: Investor dollar-weighted returns and investor flow history (subscriptions and redemptions by quarter) for every open-ended or semi-liquid vehicle.
requests.format: Administrator-produced report.
requests.why: Investors can lose money in funds with positive time-weighted returns because flows come in near the top (0.13).
requests.pass: Dollar-weighted investor returns are reported alongside time-weighted returns and the gap is explained.
requests.fail: Only time-weighted returns provided.
requests.verify: Obtain from the administrator.

requests.request: Successor-fund or platform sizing table: size of this fund or program against the funds that produced the track record, senior team size, and deals per partner.
requests.format: Table by fund.
requests.why: Size is the enemy of performance (Swensen, 0.13).
requests.pass: Any increase in fund size over the funds that earned the record is matched by a proportional increase in senior team; deals per partner do not rise.
requests.fail: Successor fund far larger than the funds that earned the record without a matching increase in senior team.
requests.verify: Confirm team size from Form ADV and references.

requests.request: Carry and GP-ownership split by person for the current and prior fund, and the vesting schedule.
requests.format: Table from the GP's governing documents.
requests.why: Underprovision of carry to non-founders predicts senior departures (founders mean 19.2% vs 10.9%) (0.13).
requests.pass: Carry is shared with the people who will do the work, with vesting; no single founder captures carry out of line with role.
requests.fail: Carry concentrated in departing or non-working founders; next generation underpaid.
requests.verify: Reconcile to the GP operating agreement.

requests.request: Forecast record: every past projection, budget or investor guidance the sponsor or management gave for prior deals or years, alongside the actual result.
requests.format: Table by deal or year, with the original projection documents attached.
requests.why: Repeated optimistic misses are a fraud precursor (a quarter of SEC AAER misstatements began as optimistic errors); executive 80% ranges capture outcomes only 36% of the time (0.2, 0.6).
requests.pass: Actuals land within the sponsor's stated ranges at a rate consistent with calibration and misses are not one-directional.
requests.fail: A pattern of repeated optimistic misses, or past projections that cannot be produced.
requests.verify: Compare with prior offering memoranda, lender reports and LP letters obtained from third parties.

requests.request: Evidence of each claimed prior exit or founder success: filings, closing statements, cap tables and distribution records showing the outcome and the principal's role.
requests.format: Third-party documents (SEC filings, closing statements, transfer-agent records).
requests.why: Prior success is a material underwriting variable (founder success about 30% after a success vs 18% first-time) and is often inflated (0.2, 0.14).
requests.pass: Every claimed exit is documented and the principal's stated role and proceeds are confirmed.
requests.fail: Claimed exits that cannot be documented or where the principal's role was minor.
requests.verify: Check SEC EDGAR, state filings and the acquirer's announcements; confirm with co-investors.

requests.request: Reference list of at least 15 contactable people across former investors, lenders, co-investors, partners, former employees, customers and vendors, including people who left on bad terms.
requests.format: Names, roles, relationship, dates and phone numbers; we add references we find independently.
requests.why: Tips detect 43% of frauds, more than half from employees and almost a third from vendors and customers (0.2).
requests.pass: We complete at least 10 reference calls (13 late-stage, 8 early-stage), at least half sourced by us, and ask each whether they were ever asked to do something with invoices, payments or records that felt wrong.
requests.fail: Only friendly references offered; references who decline or describe pressure on records, payments or invoices.
requests.verify: Source independent references from prior deal documents, LinkedIn, litigation dockets and former employers.

requests.request: Last 8 quarterly investor letters or portfolio commentaries (or lender reports for operating companies).
requests.format: Letters as sent, with dates.
requests.why: Material changes in disclosure language predict worse outcomes; early letters that dwell on refinancing and capital structure predict weaker returns (0.4, 0.13).
requests.pass: Every material change in risk, legal or financial language between letters is explained in writing.
requests.fail: Unexplained edits to risk or legal language; commentary dwelling on refinancing, covenants or capital structure.
requests.verify: Text-diff the letters ourselves and send written questions for each material edit.

requests.request: Leadership assessment for the CEO and top team against the plan: can the incumbent execute it, how gaps close, named internal and external successors, and how requirements change across the hold.
requests.format: Written assessment by the sponsor plus successor bench list.
requests.why: 69% of buyouts change CEO during the hold; team is the top factor in both successes and failures (0.14).
requests.pass: Each of the four entry questions is answered with evidence; a named successor exists for the CEO and CFO; the downside case budgets a CEO change.
requests.fail: No successor; plan depends on a single person; no budget for a leadership change.
requests.verify: Our own management interviews, references and, for control deals, an independent leadership assessment.

requests.request: Finance-function evidence: named CFO and controller with CVs, accounting policies (including revenue recognition), month-end close calendar, internal-audit or equivalent function, and an employee census reconciled to payroll.
requests.format: CVs, policy manual, close checklist, census and payroll register for the same date.
requests.why: FTX had no accounting department and no complete employee list; missing accounting function is an automatic pass (0.4).
requests.pass: In-house CFO or controller exists, census reconciles to payroll headcount and cost, and revenue recognition is documented.
requests.fail: No accounting function, census does not reconcile to payroll, or 'CFO' is a bookkeeper or controller.
requests.verify: Reconcile census to payroll provider reports obtained directly; interview the controller without the principal.

requests.request: Board and voting-control map: every director with domain expertise, independence and committee roles; voting control by class including any super-voting shares and their sunset; audit committee composition.
requests.format: Charter, voting agreements, board list with bios.
requests.why: Theranos: 100-to-1 founder votes and a board with no medical or financial expertise (0.2, 0.14).
requests.pass: At least one independent director able to chair audit; directors with domain expertise; any founder super-voting control has a sunset and is priced.
requests.fail: Founder super-voting control without sunset plus no audit committee; celebrity board without domain experts.
requests.verify: Confirm from charter filings and director interviews.

requests.request: Management and employee equity schedule, vesting terms and incentive plans.
requests.format: Option plan, grant ledger, vesting schedules.
requests.why: Misaligned incentives; PE norm is management 17% of equity (CEO 8%) (0.14).
requests.pass: Management equity and vesting are material and aligned with the plan horizon, benchmarked against 17% management / 8% CEO.
requests.fail: No management equity or fully vested at close.
requests.verify: Reconcile to the cap table and option ledger.

requests.request: Succession and key-person plan for the sponsor: who makes investment decisions, who owns investor relationships, what happens economically if a founder steps back, and whether the successor has led at scale.
requests.format: Written plan approved by the GP's governing body.
requests.why: Fewer than half of GPs have a formal transition plan; 96% of LPs call succession readiness decisive (0.14).
requests.pass: A formal transition plan exists with named successors who have led at scale.
requests.fail: No plan; founder controls all decisions and relationships.
requests.verify: Test in interviews with the successor and LP references.

requests.request: Lead investor or sponsor monitoring capacity: board seats held per partner, travel distance to the company, and partner time committed.
requests.format: Table of the deal partner's current board seats and portfolio load.
requests.why: Monitoring intensity improves outcomes (Bernstein, Giroud and Townsend, 0.14).
requests.pass: Lead partner has bandwidth (board load and proximity) to monitor actively.
requests.fail: Overloaded partner or no board seat.
requests.verify: Confirm board seats from company filings.

requests.request: For family or founder companies: independent board composition, CFO, and the outside experience of next-generation family members holding or taking board seats.
requests.format: Board list with bios; family member CVs.
requests.why: Family companies without independent oversight hide governance failures (0.14).
requests.pass: Independent director able to chair audit; a real CFO; next-generation directors with outside experience (practitioner guide 7 to 10 years and a C-level role).
requests.fail: Board wholly family-controlled with no independent director; next generation with no outside experience.
requests.verify: Interview directors and verify CVs.

requests.request: In-person access: a schedule of site visits to every material location and in-person sessions with management (not only the principal), sized to meet our written diligence floor.
requests.format: Agreed calendar with attendees.
requests.why: Refusal of on-site diligence is a universal red flag; thinner diligence widens the spread of outcomes (0.1, 0.4).
requests.pass: Diligence floor met: every material site visited and in-person management hours logged; any shortfall recorded in the memo.
requests.fail: Refusal of site visits or of access to staff below the principal.
requests.verify: We log hours, sites and references in the diligence-intensity field (0.7 item 7).

requests.request: Written answers, signed by an officer, to every question in our hints log (each data-room reference to lost customers, cancellation letters, volume declines, auditor changes, disputes or irregularities).
requests.format: Signed Q&A log with dates and the identity of the answering officer.
requests.why: Paragon Metals: the buyer saw hints but never asked the prepared questions and lost years in litigation (0.16).
requests.pass: Every hint has a written question, an answer, the asker and the date; the model is re-run for any answer that changes a number.
requests.fail: Unanswered or deflected questions; verbal answers that differ from documents.
requests.verify: Confirm answers with the third party involved (customer, auditor, lender); track refused or deflected questions as a reported field.

requests.request: Complete list of every investor, beneficial owner, borrower, guarantor, key customer, supplier, agent and counterparty in the deal chain, with full legal names, dates of birth or registration numbers, nationality and addresses, for sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening.
requests.format: Excel list in screening-ready format.
requests.why: Sanctioned persons hidden in ownership chains; OFAC 50 Percent Rule blocks entities owned 50% or more by blocked persons even if unlisted (0.3).
requests.pass: No match on OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, UN, EU and UK lists; no entity owned 50% or more in aggregate by blocked persons; PEPs identified and escalated; adverse media reviewed and cleared.
requests.fail: Confirmed sanctions match or 50%-rule block; unexplained PEP exposure; unresolved adverse media.
requests.verify: Our screening vendor screens at onboarding and continuously; ownership chains traced for the 50% rule.

requests.request: Source-of-funds evidence for the sponsor's and each principal's commitment to this deal: the specific accounts the money will come from and how it got there.
requests.format: Bank or brokerage statements for 6 or more months showing the accumulation of the funds, plus documents for any large inflows.
requests.why: Illicit or borrowed money presented as equity; a high 506(c) minimum shifts the burden to verifying the source of cash (0.3).
requests.pass: Funds trace to documented, lawful sources and are not third-party financed unless disclosed.
requests.fail: Untraceable inflows, funds from unrelated third parties, or financed equity presented as cash.
requests.verify: Statements obtained directly from the institution; large inflows traced to source documents.

requests.request: Source-of-wealth narrative for each principal and each 25%+ beneficial owner, with corroborating documents (sale agreements, tax returns, K-1s, inheritance or business records).
requests.format: Written narrative plus documents covering how total net worth was accumulated.
requests.why: Source of funds and source of wealth are different; a single bank statement is not a source-of-wealth narrative (0.3).
requests.pass: Narrative is plausible against career history and corroborated by third-party documents for the main components of wealth.
requests.fail: Wealth inconsistent with documented career; uncorroborated narrative; reliance on a single statement.
requests.verify: Corroborate against tax transcripts, public records and the background check.

requests.request: For any crypto-derived wealth or crypto counterparty: every wallet address used, and a message signed with each address's key proving control.
requests.format: Address list and signed messages over a challenge string we supply.
requests.why: OFAC's SDN list includes crypto addresses; name screening alone misses address-level exposure (0.3).
requests.pass: Each address is proven to be controlled by the person; all addresses pass OFAC address-level screening.
requests.fail: Unable to sign; address-level sanctions hit.
requests.verify: Verify signatures ourselves against our challenge string.

requests.request: Exchange account statements and the exchange's KYC records for every fiat on-ramp and off-ramp used to build crypto-derived wealth.
requests.format: Exchange-issued statements and KYC confirmations.
requests.why: On-ramp records anchor the chain of custody between fiat and crypto (0.3).
requests.pass: On-ramp accounts are in the person's name and reconcile to the traced on-chain flows.
requests.fail: On-ramps through unlicensed or high-risk exchanges, or accounts in other names.
requests.verify: Request confirmations directly from the exchange where possible.

requests.request: Sponsor's AML and sanctions compliance policy, the name of whoever performs KYC on the sponsor's other investors (GP or administrator), and whether that party files SARs.
requests.format: Policy documents, administrator services agreement, last independent AML test.
requests.why: Investment advisers have no federal AML program or SAR obligation until Jan. 1, 2028; do not assume CIP or sanctions screening was run on other LPs (0.3, 0.18).
requests.pass: A written AML and sanctions program exists, benchmarked to OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments (management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and auditing, training), with a named KYC owner.
requests.fail: No AML program and no administrator KYC on co-investors.
requests.verify: Confirm the KYC scope directly with the administrator.

requests.request: Accredited-investor or qualified-purchaser verification evidence for every investor in a 506(c) offering (tax returns, W-2s, bank statements or a licensed professional's letter), or, under the minimum-investment route, proof that the minimum ($200,000 natural persons, $1,000,000 entities) was paid in cash, not third-party financed, with a written representation.
requests.format: Verification file per investor; third-party verification letters dated within 90 days of the sale.
requests.why: 506(c) requires reasonable steps to verify, not self-certification (17 CFR 230.506(c)(2)(ii)) (0.3).
requests.pass: Every investor has documentary verification dated within 90 days, or satisfies all minimum-investment conditions with source-of-cash evidence.
requests.fail: Self-certification only; stale letters; financed minimums.
requests.verify: Sample investor files and confirm letters with the issuing professional.

requests.request: Schedule of all litigation, arbitration, regulatory proceedings, subpoenas and threatened claims in the last 10 years involving the sponsor entity, each principal and the target, with pleadings and outcomes.
requests.format: Schedule plus copies of complaints, settlements and judgments.
requests.why: 41% of funds in the ODD sample had a past legal or regulatory problem, more than twice the rate in Form ADV (0.2).
requests.pass: Schedule reconciles to our independent litigation searches in every relevant federal and state court; no undisclosed matters.
requests.fail: Undisclosed matters found in our searches; pattern of investor or lender suits.
requests.verify: Run docket searches (PACER, state courts) on the entity and every principal ourselves.

requests.request: All SEC, FINRA and state regulator correspondence in the last 5 years: exam deficiency letters and responses, Wells notices, subpoenas, consent orders.
requests.format: Copies of letters and responses.
requests.why: Regulatory problems are under-disclosed; SEC exam deficiencies are the test list for fund compliance (0.2, 0.15).
requests.pass: Every deficiency was remediated and the remediation is documented; no open Wells notice.
requests.fail: Open Wells notice, repeated deficiencies, or correspondence withheld.
requests.verify: Cross-check with BrokerCheck, IAPD and state regulator records.

requests.request: Internal investigations log for the last 3 years: every allegation, who investigated, findings and how each matter was closed.
requests.format: Log with case summaries; board or audit committee minutes where matters were reported.
requests.why: Misconduct runs about 64 times the most expansive public database; a clean public record is weak evidence (0.15).
requests.pass: Log exists, matters were investigated independently of the accused, and closures are documented.
requests.fail: No log; matters closed by the accused's chain of command; repeat issues.
requests.verify: Interview the person who runs investigations and the audit committee chair.

requests.request: Whistleblower hotline details (phone, e-mail, web) and 3 years of hotline statistics: volume, categories, anonymity rate and resolution times.
requests.format: Hotline vendor report and policy.
requests.why: One-fifth of hotlines tested were non-functional; tip-detected frauds run a median 17 months vs 24 (auditor) and 36 (law enforcement) (0.15).
requests.pass: Hotline exists, is operated independently of management, and reports volume and resolution times for 3 years.
requests.fail: No hotline, hotline routed to the CEO, or statistics unavailable.
requests.verify: We test the hotline ourselves (third-party stage).

requests.request: Compliance program documents: code of ethics, compliance manual, personal-trading and conflicts policies, gifts and entertainment, and the last annual compliance review.
requests.format: Policies and the latest annual review signed by the CCO.
requests.why: DOJ expects comprehensive pre-acquisition compliance diligence and post-close integration (0.15).
requests.pass: Program covers the business's actual risks and has been reviewed in the last 12 months.
requests.fail: No program or a template never adapted or tested.
requests.verify: Test sample controls during diligence; plan a 100-day compliance integration and audit.

requests.request: Self-assessment against the SEC exam deficiency list: LPAC consents for conflicted transactions, post-commitment fee step-downs, term extensions, strategy and leverage limits, key-person events, track-record presentation, service-provider diligence, and hedge clauses waiving fiduciary duty.
requests.format: Written response per item with supporting documents (LPAC minutes, fee calculations).
requests.why: These are recurring SEC private-fund findings (0.15).
requests.pass: Every item is documented as compliant with evidence.
requests.fail: Skipped LPAC consents, fees not stepped down, unapproved extensions ('zombie funds'), strategy or leverage outside limits, hedge clauses.
requests.verify: Test LPAC minutes and fee calculations ourselves.

requests.request: List of foreign sales agents, intermediaries, government customers, licences and permits held abroad, with agent contracts and payment histories.
requests.format: Schedule plus contracts and payment ledgers.
requests.why: Corruption appears in 45% of ACFE cases; successor liability under the FCPA (0.15).
requests.pass: Third-party and agent diligence completed; commissions consistent with services; disclosure decision planned before signing.
requests.fail: Agents with government ties, unusual commissions or payments to third countries.
requests.verify: Run agent background checks; review payments against contracts.

requests.request: Billing, coding and referral-practice documentation for government-payor or government-contract revenue, including compliance audits, overpayment refunds and any CIDs or qui tam notices.
requests.format: Policies, audit reports, refund logs.
requests.why: Sponsors face False Claims Act liability for portfolio kickback schemes (Riordan, Lewis & Haden, $21.36M) (0.15).
requests.pass: Independent billing audit finds error rates within payor tolerance; no kickback-pattern referral arrangements.
requests.fail: Referral payments tied to volume; open government investigations.
requests.verify: Independent coding and billing audit on a statistical sample.

requests.request: Multiemployer pension plan participation and estimated withdrawal liability, and the ownership structure relative to the 80% common-control threshold.
requests.format: Plan notices, actuarial withdrawal-liability estimates, ownership chart.
requests.why: Sun Capital funds were held liable for a portfolio company's withdrawal liability (0.15).
requests.pass: Withdrawal liability is quantified and ownership is structured to avoid 80% common control where liability exists.
requests.fail: Unquantified withdrawal liability; sponsor funds under common control.
requests.verify: Request estimates directly from plan administrators.

requests.request: Quality-system records for regulated manufacturing: FDA Form 483s, warning letters, recalls, audit trails, and access for an independent data-integrity audit comparing raw lab data with reported data.
requests.format: Copies of FDA correspondence and system access for the auditor.
requests.why: Akorn: falsified data found after signing (0.15).
requests.pass: No open 483 observations on data integrity; raw data reconciles to reported data in the independent audit.
requests.fail: Data-integrity observations, missing audit trails, or refusal of raw-data access.
requests.verify: Independent data-integrity audit (third-party stage).

requests.request: Franchise agreements, FDD Item 17, employment agreements and vendor contracts, reviewed for no-poach, non-solicit and wage-fixing provisions, plus non-compete agreements for key employees.
requests.format: Contract set and counsel's summary.
requests.why: About 58% of major franchisors' agreements had no-poach clauses; AG actions and class actions followed (0.15).
requests.pass: No no-poach or wage-fixing provisions remain; no open AG or class-action exposure; non-competes enforceable in each state for key employees.
requests.fail: Live no-poach clauses; pending antitrust claims.
requests.verify: Our counsel reviews the contracts and dockets.

requests.request: Exit antitrust analysis for any strategic-exit thesis: overlapping products and the HSR position of likely acquirers.
requests.format: Counsel memo.
requests.why: Killer acquisitions cluster just below HSR thresholds; expect FTC and DOJ scrutiny of sub-threshold deals (0.15).
requests.pass: The exit thesis survives antitrust review or names non-strategic buyers.
requests.fail: Exit depends on a single strategic buyer facing antitrust risk.
requests.verify: Our counsel's review.

requests.request: Trailing 36 months of bank statements for every account of the sponsor's deal entities, the issuer and every operating or asset-owning entity, plus the bank confirmations used in any QoE.
requests.format: Bank-issued PDFs or direct bank delivery; full statements with every page; list of accounts tied to the bank-confirmation responses.
requests.why: Proof of cash catches revenue and distributions that exist only on the P&L (0.5).
requests.pass: Deposits reconcile to reported revenue and outflows to reported expenses and distributions for every month; every account on the bank confirmations is in the set; no unexplained related-party transfers.
requests.fail: Gaps in months or accounts, statements produced by the sponsor rather than the bank, or unreconciled differences.
requests.verify: Obtain statements directly from each bank under signed authorization and compare with the sponsor's copies.

requests.request: Authorized-signatory list and wire-approval matrix for every account, as confirmed by the bank or the administrator (not described by the sponsor).
requests.format: Bank- or administrator-issued signatory cards and approval matrix.
requests.why: 16% of managers described the wire-signature process differently from their administrator (0.5).
requests.pass: The bank's or administrator's matrix matches the sponsor's description and requires at least two people, including one independent of the investment decision, to release funds.
requests.fail: Single-signatory release, mismatch with the administrator, or refusal to let us obtain it directly.
requests.verify: Obtain directly from the bank or administrator.

requests.request: Average daily (or intra-quarter) balances of cash, debt and assets for the last 8 quarters, alongside period-end figures.
requests.format: Schedule derived from bank and loan statements, with daily data available on request.
requests.why: Repo 105 moved up to $50B off Lehman's balance sheet at quarter-ends (0.4).
requests.pass: Period-end balances are consistent with intra-quarter averages; no recurring financing that unwinds just after period-end.
requests.fail: Period-end cash materially above, or debt materially below, intra-quarter averages; recurring quarter-end transactions.
requests.verify: Compute averages ourselves from daily bank and loan statements.

requests.request: Bank account list with balances by institution and the insured share of each, plus every pooled cash vehicle (money market funds, cash-management products, sweeps, stablecoins, tokenized cash).
requests.format: Schedule tied to bank statements; fund fact sheets and holdings for each pooled vehicle.
requests.why: SVB had 94% uninsured deposits; the Reserve Primary Fund gated and paid 99 cents only after two years (0.11).
requests.pass: Cash is spread across banks, or held in insured sweeps or Treasury MMFs; no loan covenant forces a single bank; pooled vehicles are looked through.
requests.fail: Single uninsured bank; material cash in vehicles that can gate; covenant forcing a single bank.
requests.verify: Confirm balances directly with each institution; look through MMF holdings.

requests.request: Statement of how many weeks of payroll and debt service the business could meet if its main bank closed this morning, with the supporting cash map.
requests.format: Short memo with calculation.
requests.why: SVB-type failures threaten payroll (0.11).
requests.pass: Cash outside the main bank or insured covers at least the payroll and debt service until a replacement bank is in place; plan documented.
requests.fail: Payroll depends on uninsured balances at a single bank.
requests.verify: Recompute from the bank account list.

requests.request: Audited financial statements for the last 3 years for the sponsor's vehicles and the issuer, with the auditor's engagement letters, management letters, and the auditor's PCAOB registration or peer-review report.
requests.format: Auditor-signed statements; engagement and management letters; latest peer review.
requests.why: Madoff's auditor was a two-partner firm with no peer review; non-Big 4 auditor plus internal pricing is associated with misrepresentation (0.4).
requests.pass: Unqualified opinions by an independent auditor sized to the mandate, with a clean peer review; management-letter points remediated.
requests.fail: No audit, qualified opinion, undersized or unreviewed auditor, or a non-Big 4 auditor combined with internal pricing without justification.
requests.verify: Call the audit partner directly on an independently obtained number; confirm the peer review with the AICPA or PCAOB.

requests.request: History of auditor changes, resignations, late audits, restatements and any unbooked rebates or post-closing adjustments for the last 5 years, with explanations.
requests.format: Schedule with resignation letters and restatement memos.
requests.why: Frauds start small; a late audit, restated quarter or unbooked rebate is the early signal (0.4); Cloudbreak counterparties hid an auditor resignation (0.16).
requests.pass: No unexplained auditor change, late audit or restatement.
requests.fail: Auditor resignation, repeated late audits or restatements explained away.
requests.verify: Ask the prior auditor directly why the relationship ended.

requests.request: Reconciliation of adjusted EBITDA (or any non-GAAP metric) to GAAP, with support for every add-back.
requests.format: Excel bridge with invoices, contracts or payroll evidence per add-back.
requests.why: Adjusted earnings with no GAAP reconciliation is a classic sales-side tell; losses are claimed at the deal multiple (0.4, 0.16).
requests.pass: Every add-back is documented, non-recurring and accepted by the QoE.
requests.fail: Unsupported or recurring add-backs; no GAAP reconciliation.
requests.verify: QoE tests each add-back.

requests.request: Schedule of every SPV, joint venture, guarantee, keepwell, comfort letter and 'moral obligation' support given by the sponsor, issuer or affiliates.
requests.format: Schedule plus the underlying agreements; officer certification of completeness.
requests.why: Enron's partnerships and banks' SIVs held risk off the balance sheet with implied sponsor support (0.4).
requests.pass: All off-balance-sheet support is disclosed and included in a consolidated look-through of leverage.
requests.fail: Undisclosed guarantees or vehicles found in searches or footnotes.
requests.verify: Reconcile to UCC, litigation and secretary-of-state searches and audit footnotes.

requests.request: Every factoring, supply-chain-finance, receivables-sale, inventory-finance and similar agreement of the issuer and every affiliate and principal-owned entity, with current balances.
requests.format: Executed agreements and statements from each provider.
requests.why: First Brands: reported leverage about 5x, about 20x counting factoring and supply-chain finance (0.4, Spine).
requests.pass: All such financing is disclosed, reconciles to provider statements and to what each lender is told, and is added to leverage.
requests.fail: Undisclosed facilities; balances that differ from provider statements; financing through founder-owned entities.
requests.verify: Confirm balances directly with each provider; compare with UCC search results.

requests.request: Related-party transaction schedule: every transaction, lease, loan, service agreement or payment between the sponsor, principals, their families or entities and the deal entities, for the last 3 years.
requests.format: Schedule plus agreements; officer certification.
requests.why: Steering good deals to insiders; commingling; insider leakage (Momentum Advisors) (0.4, 0.15).
requests.pass: All related-party flows are disclosed, at market terms, and approved by an independent party.
requests.fail: Undisclosed related-party payments found in bank statements.
requests.verify: Match against bank-statement counterparties.

requests.request: Statements for every account the principals control that has received or sent money to or from the deal entities or investors, and a certification that no fund or investor money passes through personal accounts.
requests.format: Bank statements and signed certification.
requests.why: Commingling of personal and fund accounts is a universal red flag (0.4).
requests.pass: No investor or entity money passes through personal accounts; all flows are documented.
requests.fail: Any commingling.
requests.verify: Trace inflows and outflows in the 36-month statements.

requests.request: Evidence that customer or fund assets are held in accounts titled to the fund or customer at a custodian outside the sponsor's group, and a reconciliation of those assets to customer liabilities.
requests.format: Custodian account-title documents and reconciliation.
requests.why: Customer assets used for other ventures (FTX); omnibus accounts complicated Lehman's broker-dealer liquidation (0.4, 0.5).
requests.pass: Assets are segregated in fund- or customer-titled accounts at an independent custodian and reconcile to liabilities.
requests.fail: Assets in sponsor-titled or omnibus accounts, or not reconciled to liabilities.
requests.verify: Confirm account title and balance directly with the custodian.

requests.request: Distribution history: every distribution paid to investors in the last 5 years, with the source account and the underlying asset or portfolio cash flow that funded it.
requests.format: Schedule tied to bank statements.
requests.why: GPB Capital paid 'portfolio cash flow' distributions from new capital (0.4, 0.5).
requests.pass: Every distribution traces to asset-level operating cash flow, not to new subscriptions or borrowing.
requests.fail: Distributions funded by new investor money (the definition of a Ponzi) or by undisclosed borrowing.
requests.verify: Trace each distribution in the bank statements.

requests.request: For returns said to come from operating assets (ATMs, machines, locations, loans, leases): an asset register with serial numbers and locations, and revenue files from the processor, servicer or counterparty.
requests.format: Asset register plus processor or servicer reports delivered directly to us.
requests.why: Heller ATM scheme: fixed 'ATM fee' distributions funded by new money (0.4, 0.5).
requests.pass: Sample assets exist on site inspection and processor revenue matches reported revenue.
requests.fail: Assets that cannot be located; revenue only from sponsor reports.
requests.verify: Obtain processor and servicer files directly; inspect a sample of assets.

requests.request: Sales by customer for the top 10 customers for 3 years, with contracts, and permission to call each customer and obtain its volume forecast.
requests.format: Customer-level revenue schedule tied to invoices and cash receipts.
requests.why: Paragon Metals: the CEO hid volume cuts by the largest customers; supplier sales growth that outruns customers' purchases predicts revenue fraud (0.4, 0.16).
requests.pass: Reported sales to each top customer are consistent with the customer's own purchase, inventory and payables trends; customer forecasts support the model.
requests.fail: Gap between reported sales growth and customer purchase growth; jumps in customer inventory or payables (channel stuffing); refusal to allow customer calls.
requests.verify: Call top customers directly; use filings or confirmations of public customers.

requests.request: Cohort data: customers acquired per period, total active customers, orders per period, retention curves, and the share of revenue from customers acquired in the period.
