requests.format: Customer-level or cohort-level data export from the system of record.
requests.why: Blue Apron: about 70% of customers churned within six months; growth made of acquisition needs ever-rising marketing spend (0.6).
requests.pass: Cohort retention is stable or improving and revenue from new customers is not rising as a share of revenue relative to prior cohorts.
requests.fail: Steep cohort decay or a 'hockey stick made entirely of acquisition'.
requests.verify: Rebuild cohorts from raw transaction data.

requests.request: Borrower- or tenant-level income verification for any pool underwritten on stated income: IRS transcripts (Form 4506-C), payroll records or bank deposits.
requests.format: Transcripts or third-party income evidence for a sample sized by our credit team.
requests.why: In 2002 to 2005 stated mortgage income in fraud-plagued zip codes ran about 90% above IRS income (0.4).
requests.pass: Stated income reconciles to IRS or payroll data and pool income growth does not outrun local IRS SOI or BLS wage growth.
requests.fail: Stated income above verified income; pool income growth outrunning local benchmarks.
requests.verify: Order transcripts ourselves via 4506-C.

requests.request: Loan-tape distributions of FICO, DTI and other eligibility variables, and default rates around every eligibility cutoff.
requests.format: Loan-level tape in Excel or CSV.
requests.why: Loans just above securitization cutoffs defaulted 10% to 25% more; bunching at cutoffs signals origination gaming (0.10).
requests.pass: No bunching or performance jump at any cutoff.
requests.fail: Bunching or a default jump at a cutoff.
requests.verify: Plot distributions ourselves from the tape.

requests.request: Borrower-level payment history traced to bank deposits and a delinquency roll-rate report for any claim of low defaults.
requests.format: Servicing-system export and bank deposit reconciliation.
requests.why: First Liberty Building & Loan: 'few defaults' claims hid a Ponzi (0.5).
requests.pass: Payments in the servicing system reconcile to bank deposits and delinquency rolls support the stated default rate.
requests.fail: Payments not found in deposits; roll rates inconsistent with claims.
requests.verify: Reconcile a sample against bank statements.

requests.request: For any public target, take-private, carve-out from a public parent or public borrower: the last 8 quarters of 10-K and 10-Q filings with management's explanation of every material change in risk factors, MD&A and legal proceedings.
requests.format: Filings plus written explanations.
requests.why: Firms that materially change filing language later show lower earnings and higher bankruptcy risk (Lazy Prices) (0.4).
requests.pass: Every material edit is explained and the explanation is consistent with the model.
requests.fail: Unexplained or evasive explanations of edits to risk factors or legal proceedings.
requests.verify: Diff the filings ourselves.

requests.request: Assumption source log: for every key model input, the source document, who produced it, and whether it is a sponsor or management figure.
requests.format: Table keyed to model input cells.
requests.why: Anchoring: committees re-label the sponsor's figure as their own (0.12 bias question 7).
requests.pass: Every key input has a source; sponsor figures are identified and independently tested.
requests.fail: Inputs with no source.
requests.verify: Trace a sample of inputs to source documents.

requests.request: Management forecast alongside the sponsor's base case, with the haircut applied stated explicitly.
requests.format: Model tab with both cases.
requests.why: Median PE discount to management EBITDA forecasts is 20%; executive 80% ranges capture outcomes only 36% of the time (0.6, 0.7).
requests.pass: Base case applies an explicit haircut of about 20% to management's forecast, or justifies a smaller one with the forecast record.
requests.fail: Base case equals management's forecast.
requests.verify: Compare with the forecast record.

requests.request: Downside case built from base rates (the outcome distribution of a reference class of similar deals), with sponsor ranges widened about 2x.
requests.format: Model tab with the reference class cited.
requests.why: Management downside cases are midpoints, not floors (0.6, 0.12).
requests.pass: Downside case uses an outside-view base rate and the deal still meets its minimum hurdle or covenant tests.
requests.fail: Downside is the base case with a small haircut, or the deal fails at base-rate outcomes.
requests.verify: We rebuild the downside ourselves.

requests.request: Flat-margin base case, or a costed line-by-line bridge naming every efficiency that expands margins.
requests.format: Model tab or cost bridge.
requests.why: Margins do not expand with scale on average (6,103 IPO firms, 1975 to 2016) (0.6).
requests.pass: Base case holds margins flat unless each efficiency is costed and evidenced.
requests.fail: Margin expansion assumed from scale without a costed bridge.
requests.verify: Test each efficiency with operations diligence.

requests.request: Exit cases: exit multiple equal to or below entry; entry minus 1 to 2 turns; and exit equal to entry with margins flat.
requests.format: Model scenarios with returns for each.
requests.why: Search-fund value creation was about 80% multiple expansion; exit = entry is not conservative at a cyclical peak (0.6, 0.7).
requests.pass: The deal clears its hurdle with exit equal to entry and margins flat, and shows the return at entry minus 1 to 2 turns.
requests.fail: Return depends on multiple expansion.
requests.verify: Recompute in our copy of the model.

requests.request: Reverse valuation ('what must be true'): the steady-state margin, growth and exit multiple the price implies, on a fully diluted share count.
requests.format: Model tab.
requests.why: Adding RSUs and options moved one implied valuation from $1.25T to about $1.7T (0.6).
requests.pass: Implied margin, growth and multiple are within the range achieved by peers and historical high-growth companies.
requests.fail: Price requires outcomes no peer has achieved.
requests.verify: Benchmark against peers ourselves.

requests.request: Return attribution for this deal's base case: earnings growth, debt paydown, multiple change and any dividend recap, as separate lines.
requests.format: Model bridge.
requests.why: A memo that cannot separate these asks the committee to approve a hope (0.7 item 6).
requests.pass: Most of the base-case return comes from earnings growth; levers align with what the industry says works (revenue growth, incentives, governance).
requests.fail: Return relies on cost cuts or multiple arbitrage.
requests.verify: Recompute.

requests.request: Stress cases from outside the deal: +200 bp on debt cost and discount rate; stressed advance rates and haircuts; failure of the main bank, lender or counterparty.
requests.format: Model scenarios.
requests.why: Long-duration assets are rate-sensitive; advance rates and counterparties fail together in a downturn (0.7, 0.11, 0.19).
requests.pass: Deal meets debt service and covenants under +200 bp and a counterparty-failure case, or the shortfall is funded.
requests.fail: Covenant breach or liquidity shortfall under the stress with no funding plan.
requests.verify: Run in our copy of the model.

requests.request: Re-underwriting of every debt maturing within 48 months at the current market rate, with the refinancing gap and who funds it.
requests.format: Debt schedule and refinance scenario.
requests.why: Refinancing walls: legacy coupons near 1% against market near 7% (0.10).
requests.pass: Refinance gap is sized and a committed or credible funding source is named.
requests.fail: Unfunded refinancing gap.
requests.verify: Price indicative refinancing with lenders ourselves.

requests.request: Leverage justification: target leverage set against the cash-flow volatility of the business, not what lenders will provide.
requests.format: Memo with historical cash-flow volatility and coverage at stressed cash flow.
requests.why: About two-thirds of PE firms set leverage at what the market will bear (0.10).
requests.pass: Coverage holds at a historical-worst cash-flow year.
requests.fail: Leverage justified only by lender appetite.
requests.verify: Recompute from historicals.

requests.request: Credit agreement and a calculation of maximum permitted leverage under every basket, ratio-debt capacity and EBITDA add-back, against leverage at close.
requests.format: Executed or draft credit agreement and our counsel's basket calculation.
requests.why: Over 70% of contracts permit senior secured debt above 5x; median agreement has 8 baskets (0.7, 0.10).
requests.pass: Maximum permitted leverage is disclosed and does not let priming debt subordinate our position.
requests.fail: Maximum permitted far above closing leverage; J.Crew-style unrestricted-subsidiary leakage.
requests.verify: Our own counsel reviews baskets, EBITDA definition and unrestricted-subsidiary provisions.

requests.request: Synergy table for any M&A or add-on: probability weights and timing, cost synergies separate from revenue synergies, and a dis-synergy line (lost customers and talent).
requests.format: Model tab.
requests.why: 70% to 90% of deals underperform expectations; revenue synergies take 2 to 3+ years (0.7).
requests.pass: Synergies are probability-weighted, timed (cost 1 to 2 years, revenue 2 to 3+), and the deal clears its hurdle without revenue synergies.
requests.fail: Unweighted synergies; no dis-synergies.
requests.verify: Test with operating diligence.

requests.request: Any claimed real-option value (growth options, abandonment value) as a separate, ranged line.
requests.format: Model tab with explicit assumptions.
requests.why: Option value used to rationalize price (0.6).
requests.pass: Deal clears its hurdle without the option line.
requests.fail: Price depends on option value.
requests.verify: Review assumptions.

requests.request: Valuation of the specific security we are buying (liquidation preferences, ratchets, participation, seniority), and any prior-round marks repriced against current comparables with a down-round case.
requests.format: Waterfall model and comparables.
requests.why: Headline post-money valuations are biased upward; 2021 marks need repricing (0.6).
requests.pass: Our security's value is computed from the waterfall, not the headline post-money.
requests.fail: Pricing off headline post-money.
requests.verify: Rebuild the waterfall.

requests.request: Downside case for consumer exposure: revenue growth 2 points lower for 3 years if the 3-year change in household debt to GDP for the relevant market is in the top third of history.
requests.format: Model scenario citing BIS or Fed Z.1 data.
requests.why: Household-debt booms predict busts (Mian, Sufi and Verner) (0.10).
requests.pass: Deal meets its hurdle or covenants under the case.
requests.fail: Fails under the household-debt downside.
requests.verify: We pull the data ourselves.

requests.request: Real-asset value cross-checks: exit cap rate and current appraisal cap against the REIT-implied cap rate for the property type, a CAPM and BBB/BB-yield comparison, Gordon growth, and inflation-only real growth in exit values.
requests.format: Valuation memo.
requests.why: Appraisals lag public markets (REIT-implied 5.74% vs ODCE 4.47%, Q2 2026); long-run real prices are near flat (0.6, 0.10).
requests.pass: Exit cap is at or above the REIT-implied cap; exit values grow at inflation only unless a supply constraint is documented.
requests.fail: Exit cap below public-implied caps; real growth assumed.
requests.verify: Pull REIT-implied caps ourselves.

requests.request: Credit valuation inputs: recovery assumptions by priority, spread decomposition, and the same loan's marks in other holders' public schedules of investments.
requests.format: Memo with sources.
requests.why: Recoveries by priority (loans 84%, secured bonds 60%, unsecured 38%); BDC marks lag by four quarters (0.6).
requests.pass: Recovery assumptions at or below the priority anchors; marks consistent with other holders' marks.
requests.fail: Recovery above anchors; marks above other BDCs' marks for the same loan.
requests.verify: Check BDC Schedules of Investments ourselves.

requests.request: Default and loss statistics quoted by the sponsor, with the definition of each (covenant default, payment default, realized loss) and the source.
requests.format: Written note.
requests.why: Covenant-default indices (about 2.4% to 2.7%) and realized-loss series (about 1.0% a year) measure different things (0.10).
requests.pass: Each quoted rate names its definition and source and is compared with like-for-like benchmarks.
requests.fail: Rates quoted without a definition.
requests.verify: Compare with Proskauer and Cliffwater series.

requests.request: Expected net alpha for this commitment, the benchmark it is measured against (PME vs a levered small-value index for buyouts) and how prior predictions for this GP compared with outcomes.
requests.format: Written note.
requests.why: PE alpha for the average investor is about zero; break-even alpha equals GP compensation (0.13).
requests.pass: Expected net alpha is positive against a risk-matched benchmark and supported by prior realized outcomes.
requests.fail: No benchmark or alpha that disappears against a levered small-value index.
requests.verify: Recompute ourselves.

requests.request: Currency and peg analysis: currency of revenue, costs and debt, and hedges for any mismatch.
requests.format: Schedule and hedge confirmations.
requests.why: Dollar debt against peg-dependent revenue lost every dollar in Argentina (0.11).
requests.pass: No unhedged mismatch between revenue and debt currencies, or the downside case absorbs a devaluation.
requests.fail: Unhedged mismatch.
requests.verify: Confirm hedges with counterparties.

requests.request: Every financing line (subscription, NAV, warehouse, repo, margin, asset-based, revolver) with its haircut or advance rate, margin-call mechanics, triggers and term.
requests.format: Executed agreements and current borrowing-base certificates.
requests.why: Repo haircuts went from about zero to nearly 50%; margins from 10% to above 40% (0.10, 0.11).
requests.pass: With haircuts stressed to 50% for non-Treasury structured collateral and 100% for esoteric assets, unencumbered liquidity covers the call.
requests.fail: Liquidity shortfall under stressed haircuts.
requests.verify: Confirm terms and balances with each lender.

requests.request: Liquidity-spiral stress for any levered vehicle: simultaneous 20% to 30% collateral price fall plus a haircut increase, the order of asset sales, and covenant effects elsewhere.
requests.format: Model output.
requests.why: Margin and loss spirals make liquidity vanish across assets at once (0.10).
requests.pass: Vehicle survives without forced sales that breach covenants elsewhere.
requests.fail: Forced sales or cross-defaults.
requests.verify: Run in our copy of the model.

requests.request: Fund-level leverage stack: subscription line, NAV facility and asset-based facilities, with each lender, size, margin-call trigger and LPA consent provisions for NAV debt and GP-leds.
requests.format: Facility agreements and LPA sections.
requests.why: Bank lending to private-credit vehicles rose from about $8B to about $95B; NAV loans can pay carry on borrowed distributions (0.10, 0.13).
requests.pass: Full stack disclosed with triggers; NAV debt and GP-leds require LPAC or LP consent.
requests.fail: Undisclosed facilities; no consent requirement.
requests.verify: Confirm with lenders.

requests.request: Hedge and derivative schedule: counterparties, ISDA and CSA terms, close-out netting, collateral-posting triggers, and whether each swap is secured pari passu under the credit agreement.
requests.format: Schedule plus ISDAs and confirmations.
requests.why: Lehman had 906,000 derivatives under 6,120 ISDAs; ISDA documentation is not a resolution plan (0.11).
requests.pass: Counterparties mapped; netting enforceable; swap secured pari passu; collateral triggers funded.
requests.fail: Concentrated weak counterparties or unfunded collateral triggers.
requests.verify: Confirm with each counterparty.

requests.request: Custodian and prime-broker list, with each counterparty's credit indicators and a documented plan to move assets and novate trades.
requests.format: List and contingency plan.
requests.why: Credit Suisse outflows and CDS above 1,000 bp preceded its takeover (0.11).
requests.pass: A tested plan to move assets exists and no single counterparty failure stops the vehicle.
requests.fail: No plan; concentration in a stressed counterparty.
requests.verify: Monitor CDS and public data.

requests.request: Aggregate exposure across all prime brokers and swap counterparties for any co-investor or vehicle using total-return swaps or margin.
requests.format: Statement from each counterparty.
requests.why: Archegos: no prime broker saw the whole book; banks lost more than $10B (0.4, 0.11).
requests.pass: Aggregate exposure across all counterparties is disclosed and within limits.
requests.fail: Only one counterparty's view available.
requests.verify: Obtain statements directly.

requests.request: Cash-collateral reinvestment policy and every collateral-posting trigger (rating downgrade, mark-to-market).
requests.format: Policy and agreements.
requests.why: AIG reinvested securities-lending cash in RMBS and faced CDS collateral calls (0.11).
requests.pass: Cash collateral held in liquid assets; triggers modelled and funded.
requests.fail: Illiquid reinvestment; unfunded triggers.
requests.verify: Review agreements.

requests.request: HTM and AFS fair-value marks and a liquidity stress (not only a loss-rate stress) for any financial counterparty or credit vehicle.
requests.format: Stress-test report with multiple scenarios.
requests.why: SVB's unrealized losses exceeded book equity; stress tests must cover funding and liquidity (0.11).
requests.pass: Multiple scenarios; stressed fair value of all securities including HTM; liquidity holds.
requests.fail: Single scenario; HTM losses ignored.
requests.verify: Recompute from statements.

requests.request: For any bank-like counterparty or lender: uninsured share of funding, unrealized securities losses against equity, IRRBB (economic value of equity under rate shocks), a 30-day LCR-style outflow test, and collateral pre-positioned at the Fed.
requests.format: Call reports or financial statements and the lender's own metrics.
requests.why: SVB: 94% uninsured, $17B unrealized loss vs $15B equity; Signature lacked pre-positioned collateral (0.11).
requests.pass: Unrealized losses well below equity, moderate uninsured share, and outflow coverage for 30 days.
requests.fail: Unrealized losses near or above equity; high uninsured funding.
requests.verify: Pull call reports ourselves.

requests.request: For any construction, bridge or revolving commitment from a regional or bank-like lender: the lender's funding mix and provisions making the commitment survive lender failure (replacement lender, assignment rights).
requests.format: Commitment letter and credit agreement sections.
requests.why: First Republic's failure; draw commitments that die with the lender (0.11).
requests.pass: Commitment survives lender failure through assignment or replacement rights.
requests.fail: Commitment terminates or becomes unfundable on lender failure, with no replacement lender or assignment right.
requests.verify: Our counsel reviews the commitment and credit agreement; we check the lender's call report for funding mix.

requests.request: For insurer counterparties or insurer-affiliated managers: statutory statements of the operating insurer and affiliated reinsurers, Schedule S ceded reinsurance, consolidated RBC including captives, affiliated-transaction policy, and the NAIC designation source for private placements.
requests.format: Statutory filings and policies.
requests.why: Shadow reinsurance cut average RBC by about 53 points (0.11).
requests.pass: Consolidated RBC remains adequate after including affiliated captives; affiliated placements independently valued.
requests.fail: RBC inadequate on a consolidated basis; affiliated placements self-rated.
requests.verify: Pull NAIC filings.

requests.request: For stablecoins or tokenized cash held as treasury or collateral: reserve composition at the instrument level, attestation date and auditor, custodian list, encumbrance status, and redemption terms for non-retail holders.
requests.format: Issuer reports and attestations.
requests.why: Money-like products run once a peg breaks; GENIUS Act coins must be 1:1 HQLA-backed and unencumbered (0.11, 0.18).
requests.pass: Reserves 1:1 in HQLA, audited, unencumbered, redeemable on stated terms.
requests.fail: Offshore or unregulated coins that cannot show this.
requests.verify: Check attestations directly.

requests.request: For semi-liquid vehicles: gate, suspension and in-kind provisions; redemption-queue history; liquidity coverage (cash + NII + maturities against the redemption cap); mark-lag tests.
requests.format: Offering documents and administrator reports.
requests.why: Q2 2026 semi-liquid private credit had its first net outflow with $10.7B unmet; recurring 5% redemptions exhaust liquidity (0.11).
requests.pass: Liquidity coverage exceeds the redemption cap and stale-NAV risk is managed.
requests.fail: Redemption rights above liquidity coverage; queue history of gating.
requests.verify: Recompute from statements.

requests.request: Sponsor's uncalled capital and reserve policy in the fund that owns the company.
requests.format: Fund statements and reserve policy.
requests.why: PE-backed companies with resource-rich sponsors weathered 2008 to 2009 better (0.11).
requests.pass: Reserves sufficient to support the company in the downside case.
requests.fail: No reserves.
requests.verify: Confirm with the administrator.

requests.request: Limit-breach log and record of limit changes for the last 24 months, and the CRO's reporting line and tenure.
requests.format: Risk committee records.
requests.why: Lehman raised limits to fit positions and replaced its CRO with a dealmaker (0.12).
requests.pass: No pattern of limits raised to fit positions; CRO independent and stable.
requests.fail: Limits raised after breaches; CRO replaced by a dealmaker.
requests.verify: Interview the CRO.

requests.request: Valuation policy, valuation-committee minutes for 3 years, the named valuation firm's or pricing service's engagement letter, and a list of who has write access to pricing inputs.
requests.format: Documents plus system access logs.
requests.why: Infinity Q manipulated 'independent' model inputs; SQN's principal prepared the only valuations while claiming an expert (0.6).
requests.pass: Independent valuer engaged and contactable; minutes show dissent and challenge; the manager cannot alter pricing inputs.
requests.fail: No engagement letter; valuer denies role; principal has write access to inputs.
requests.verify: Call the valuation firm; obtain the administrator's independent price for a sample of Level 3 positions.

requests.request: Fee and expense allocation policy and a 3-year schedule of all portfolio-company fees (monitoring, transaction, director, operating-partner) with offset calculations and broken-deal expense allocation across funds and co-investors.
requests.format: Policy and Excel schedule.

requests.request: Water supply evidence: will-serve letter, water source and seniority of rights, cooling design, and water cost at post-2026 tiered pricing.

requests.pass: Eligibility confirmed and a no-credit downside passes.

requests.pass: Returns filed, consistent with financial statements; no open disputes unprovided for.

requests.request: Wire-instruction and principal-instruction verification protocol, including call-back to independently obtained numbers and controls against synthetic voice or video.

requests.fail: Instructions acted on by message alone.

requests.request: IT and cybersecurity overview: systems of record, access controls over financial and pricing systems, incident history for 3 years.

requests.pass: Segregated access; no unremediated incidents.
requests.fail: Shared admin access to financial systems.
requests.verify: Review access logs.

requests.request: For high-growth projections: a build that starts from the expected long-run size of the market and the company's share of it and works back to today, benchmarked against the paths of historical high-growth companies.
requests.format: Model tab with market-size sources and a benchmark set of historical high-growth companies.
requests.why: Extrapolating history overstates high-growth values; start from the long-run state (Wessels, 0.6).

requests.fail: Terminal share or growth path beyond anything in the benchmark set; market size from the sponsor only.

requests.request: Reference class for this deal: a list of comparable deals (asset, vintage, structure) and their actual outcome distribution, including losses, used to test the base and worst cases.
requests.format: Table with sources for each outcome.
requests.why: Answer 'is the base case too optimistic' and 'is the worst case bad enough' with an outside-view base rate, not the sponsor's scenarios (0.12, A.4 questions 10 and 11).
requests.pass: Base case sits at or below the median outcome of the reference class; worst case is at or below its bottom decile.
requests.fail: No reference class, or one made only of successes.
requests.verify: We build our own reference class and compare.

requests.request: Model of the deal's bank and warehouse facility renewal under stress: advance-rate cuts and non-renewal at the same time as the asset-price decline.
requests.format: Model scenario with each facility's renewal date and stressed terms.
requests.why: Bubbles financed by banks are the dangerous ones; the lender will be under stress exactly when you need it (Brunnermeier, Rother and Schnabel, 0.10).
requests.pass: Deal survives non-renewal of its largest facility plus a stressed advance rate during the downside price case.
requests.fail: Facility renewal assumed on current terms; no alternative funding.
requests.verify: Confirm renewal dates and terms with each lender.

requests.request: For any credit or structured position: marks against observable market indices, and explanation of any model-only mark that departs from them.
requests.format: Mark schedule with index references.
requests.why: Market-index marks have fundamental content even in a panic; model-only marks that ignore them are not defensible (0.6).
requests.pass: Marks are consistent with observable indices or departures are explained with evidence.
requests.fail: Model-only marks above observable indices.
requests.verify: Compare with index levels and other holders' marks.

requests.request: Quartile history of the sponsor's last three funds against a named, vintage-matched benchmark.
requests.format: Table with benchmark source and extraction date.
requests.why: Wharton allocators decline managers whose recent funds land consistently in the third or fourth quartile; selection is the main decision given dispersion (0.13).
requests.pass: Recent funds are not consistently third or fourth quartile.
requests.fail: Consistent third- or fourth-quartile results.
requests.verify: Pull the benchmark ourselves.

requests.request: For 'hot market' entries: a downside case widened for the vintage, not validated by the round's price.
requests.format: Model scenario.
requests.why: Startups first funded in hot markets fail more often and are valued higher, even by experienced VCs (Nanda and Rhodes-Kropf, 0.10).
requests.pass: Downside widened beyond the sponsor's and the deal still clears its minimum hurdle.
requests.fail: Round price cited as validation.
requests.verify: We set the widened case.

requests.request: Cooperate with our independent background-check firm on the sponsor entity, each principal, the CFO, controller, wire releaser, and every placement agent and salesperson: criminal (county, state, federal), civil litigation, bankruptcy, judgments and liens, regulatory (SEC, FINRA BrokerCheck, state securities regulators), adverse media, employment and education verification.
requests.format: Report issued by a firm we engage directly to us; sponsor supplies consents, prior addresses and aliases.
requests.why: 10% of managers would have passed as clean on DDQ and voluntary disclosure and were caught only by the independent check; fraud is usually collusive (0.2).
requests.pass: No undisclosed material finding in any category for any person; every finding reconciles to the signed self-disclosure and Form ADV.
requests.fail: Undisclosed criminal, fraud, securities or regulatory history; unverifiable employment or education; findings on second-tier executives or sales agents.
requests.verify: The firm reports to us, not the sponsor; we compare findings item by item to the self-disclosure questionnaire and record verbal-versus-written discrepancies.

requests.request: Provide full access for our Quality-of-Earnings provider, including the data needed for proof of cash across every bank account on the bank confirmations, and deliver the final QoE with its engagement letter and scope section.
requests.format: QoE engaged by us (or reliance letter if sponsor-commissioned); engagement type stated as SSAE No. 19 agreed-upon procedures (AT-C 215) or CS 100 consulting.
requests.why: A QoE gives no opinion or assurance; the engaging party accepts responsibility for the sufficiency of procedures, so what was not tested matters (0.5).
requests.pass: Proof of cash covers every account on the bank confirmations for the full 36 months; scope exclusions are listed and each is covered by other work in this packet; adjusted EBITDA accepted with documented add-backs.
requests.fail: Accounts excluded from proof of cash; material unexplained cash-to-revenue differences; key areas outside scope with no other coverage.
requests.verify: Read the engagement letter and scope section first; ask the provider directly what was not tested.

requests.request: Allow direct, unsolicited confirmations to be sent by us to every bank, custodian, lender, servicer and processor for balances, custody holdings, asset existence, loan balances and signatories as of a date we choose.
requests.format: Confirmation requests sent by us to contacts we obtain independently; responses returned directly to us.
requests.why: Madoff's rule: 'You must do a third-party check. It's an absolute must... It's accounting 101' (0.4, 0.5).
requests.pass: Every confirmation is returned and agrees with the sponsor's records and the 36-month statements.
requests.fail: Any confirmation that disagrees, is not returned, or is routed back through the sponsor.
requests.verify: Obtain institution contact details from public directories, not from the sponsor; follow up non-responses by phone.

requests.request: Arrange calls for us with the fund administrator, auditor and prime broker (and any custodian) in which each confirms its engagement, the wire-approval matrix, the pricing process, account control and the investor KYC it performs.
requests.format: Calls on numbers we obtain independently; written follow-up from each provider.
requests.why: 1 fund in 6 described its cash controls differently from its administrator; 3.6% disagreed on pricing (0.5).
requests.pass: Each provider confirms it is engaged and that its descriptions of wire authority, pricing and KYC match the sponsor's.
requests.fail: Provider unaware of engagement, descriptions that do not match, or sponsor refusal to arrange calls.
requests.verify: We dial out ourselves and record discrepancies in the A.2 wire-authority field.

requests.request: Sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening report on every party in the deal chain, with ownership traced for the OFAC 50 Percent Rule and address-level screening of any crypto addresses.
requests.format: Vendor report run by us against OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, UN, EU and UK lists, PEP databases and global media.
requests.why: Name screening alone misses blocked ownership chains and sanctioned addresses (0.3).
requests.pass: No unresolved hit; every potential match cleared with documented reasoning; no entity 50% or more owned in aggregate by blocked persons.
requests.fail: Confirmed hit, 50%-rule block, sanctioned address exposure, or unresolved adverse media.
requests.verify: Vendor engaged by us; rerun at closing and continuously.

requests.request: On-chain tracing report for every wallet tied to crypto-derived wealth or a crypto counterparty, covering full history to fiat on-ramps with mixer, darknet, sanctioned-address and high-risk-exchange exposure.
requests.format: Report from a blockchain-analytics vendor engaged by us, with methodology and heuristics disclosed.

requests.pass: No sanctioned or darknet exposure; any mixer or privacy-protocol exposure escalated and the judgment documented in writing.
requests.fail: Sanctioned-address or darknet exposure; undocumented mixer exposure; history that cannot be traced to a fiat on-ramp.
requests.verify: Vendor reports to us; we reconcile to exchange statements.

requests.request: UCC, federal and state tax lien, judgment and title searches across the issuer, every affiliate and every entity personally owned by the principals, in every state of organization and asset location.

requests.why: First Brands' pledges sat in affiliates and founder-owned entities the lenders did not search (0.4, 0.5).
requests.pass: Every filing matches the disclosed claims schedule; no undisclosed secured party, lien or judgment.
requests.fail: Undisclosed secured parties or filings against affiliates or principal-owned entities.
requests.verify: We order the searches using the debtor names from the certified org chart and our own secretary-of-state pulls.

requests.pass: Zero duplicate items across facilities.
requests.fail: Any duplicate pledge.
requests.verify: Agent obtains borrowing bases directly from each lender.

requests.pass: Every sampled receivable is confirmed by the debtor for amount and terms, and remittances arrive in the lockbox.
requests.fail: Unconfirmed or disputed receivables; remittances diverted.
requests.verify: We contact debtors on independently obtained numbers.

requests.format: Call notes with names, dates and questions asked.

requests.pass: No reference reports misconduct, pressure on records, or material contradiction of the sponsor's account.

requests.verify: References sourced from litigation dockets, prior deal documents, former employers and LinkedIn.

requests.pass: Hotline answers, accepts an anonymous report, and routes outside management.

requests.pass: Every named party confirms the claimed relationship, its scope and any validation performed.
requests.fail: Any denial, downgrade or refusal to confirm.
requests.verify: Contacts obtained independently.

requests.pass: Error rate within payor tolerance and no kickback-pattern referral relationships.
requests.fail: Systematic upcoding or referral payments.

requests.pass: Each A.5 field at or better than its base rate, or resolved in writing.
requests.fail: Any unresolved A.5 flag (misrepresentation, wire mismatch, refused questions).

requests.pass: Our independent value supports the price; the sponsor's named valuer confirms its role and scope.
requests.fail: Independent value below price; named valuer denies or narrows its role.
requests.verify: We call the valuer on an independently obtained number.

requests.format: Reports from consultants we engage.

requests.pass: No unmitigated finding; costs of mitigation in the model.
requests.fail: Material contamination or climate exposure without mitigation.
requests.verify: Consultants engaged by us.

requests.pass: Coverage adequate and bindable; 2x premium stress passes.
requests.fail: Coverage gaps (D&O at either level, crime, cyber), insurer of last resort, or indications only.
requests.verify: Broker engaged by us obtains quotes directly from insurers.

requests.format: Counsel memo.
requests.why: Sponsor-designated lenders' counsel face pressure not to over-lawyer (0.16).
requests.pass: Counsel signs off with no open gating issue.
requests.fail: Open issues on priming, leakage or remedies.
requests.verify: Counsel engaged and paid by us.

requests.format: Assessor report.
requests.why: Team is cited as the top factor in 96% of successes and 92% of failures (0.14).
requests.pass: Leadership can execute the plan or the gap has a funded fix.
requests.fail: Material capability gap without a successor.
requests.verify: Assessor engaged by us.

requests.request: Definitive documents containing a specific representation for every fact we could not verify, a special indemnity for every known issue found in diligence, and specific closing conditions rather than reliance on a general MAE.
requests.format: Execution versions with our counsel's mapping table (unverified fact to rep, indemnity or condition).
requests.why: R&W insurance excludes what the buyer knows; Akorn's agreement did not carve out diligence-disclosed matters (0.15, 0.16).
requests.pass: Every item on the 'could not verify' list maps to a rep, indemnity or closing condition; every known issue is priced or specially indemnified.
requests.fail: Unverified facts left uncovered; known issues left to an excluded R&W policy or a general MAE.
requests.verify: Counsel's mapping table reviewed at IC.

requests.request: Survival and limitations schedule: survival period of each rep, R&W policy period, indemnity claim deadlines and the fraud limitations period, diarized at signing.
requests.format: Schedule with dates.
requests.why: 51% of R&W claims are notified more than 12 months after closing and 24% after 24 months; Cloudbreak's fraud claim was time-barred (0.16).
requests.pass: Fundamental and financial-statement reps survive at least 24 months, or the R&W policy covers the gap; all deadlines diarized.
requests.fail: 12-month survival with no other cover; deadlines not diarized.
requests.verify: Counsel confirms against the executed documents.

requests.request: R&W insurance binder or policy with its exclusions list, retention, limit, policy period, and the diligence reports the underwriter relied on.
requests.format: Bound policy and underwriting call notes.
requests.why: Policies exclude anything known to the buyer or its advisers, so whatever diligence finds is uninsured; insured buyers may diligence less (0.16).
requests.pass: Limit about 10% to 20% of deal value, retention about 1%, premium about 2% to 3% of limit; every diligence finding is priced or covered by a special indemnity; no deal-specific exclusion swallows a gating workstream.
requests.fail: Known issues left to the policy; exclusions covering the QoE, top-customer or compliance areas that drive about three-quarters of insured loss.
requests.verify: Our counsel and broker review the exclusions against the findings list.

requests.request: Earnout provisions with objective metric definitions and worked examples, an explicit efforts standard or fixed spend commitment, buyer reporting and audit rights, rules on cost allocation, staffing and working capital during the period, acceleration triggers, expert-not-arbitrator scope, and records-of-efforts obligations.
requests.format: Execution language.
requests.why: Fortis v. J&J: the negotiated efforts definition let the buyer calibrate effort; dispute risk rises with earnout share and length (median 31% of closing payment, 24 months) (0.16).
requests.pass: Every element of the drafting checklist is present.
requests.fail: Vague 'commercially reasonable efforts', no audit rights, no acceleration triggers.
requests.verify: Counsel review against the 0.16 checklist.

requests.request: Where we receive stock as consideration: our own QoE on the stock issuer, auditor contacts and auditor-change history, solvency evidence, and net cash per share.
requests.format: Our QoE report, auditor call notes, net-cash-per-share calculation.
requests.why: Cloudbreak relied on the counterparty banker's presentations that omitted insolvency and an auditor resignation; de-SPACs delivered a mean $4.10 of cash per $10 share (0.16, A.2).
requests.pass: The stock issuer passes the same financial tests as a target; no unexplained auditor change; net cash per share computed and priced.
requests.fail: Auditor resignation, insolvency indicators, or net cash per share far below the issue price.
requests.verify: We commission the work and call the auditor directly.

requests.request: Executed LPA or side letter containing quarterly fee and performance statements, an annual audit, a fairness opinion on any GP-led secondary, LPAC consent on conflicted transactions, NAV loans and GP-leds, key-person dissolution or suspension, for-cause and no-fault removal.
requests.format: Execution versions.
requests.why: No federal rule requires these since the Private Fund Adviser rules were vacated on June 5, 2024 (0.16, 0.18).
requests.pass: Every listed protection is in the executed documents.
requests.fail: Any protection missing, or available only at GP discretion.
requests.verify: Counsel confirms against the executed documents.

requests.request: For insider-led, bridge or rescue financings: pricing evidence against our own recent marks and bridges, the record of every rejected alternative, the time and data given to non-participants, and disclosure of insider benefits.
requests.format: Board materials and minutes.
requests.why: Insider-led rescues face entire-fairness review (Guilbeau v. Footprint); veto rights used to harm the company create liability (Zync v. Porsche) (0.16).
requests.pass: Process documented on each element.
requests.fail: Insider pricing below own marks without explanation; alternatives undocumented.
requests.verify: Counsel reviews the record.

requests.request: Bring-down of sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening and of the background checks, run immediately before funding.
requests.format: Vendor bring-down report dated within the week of funding.
requests.why: Screening must be at onboarding and continuous (0.3).
requests.pass: No new sanctions hit, PEP change or adverse finding on any party since the original screen.
requests.fail: Any new hit or finding; funding stops until it is cleared.
requests.verify: Vendor engaged by us runs the bring-down; results reviewed by our compliance officer before release.

requests.request: Funding wire instructions confirmed by call-back to an independently obtained number before any money is released.
requests.format: Call-back record signed by two of our staff.
requests.why: AI-personalized deception (synthetic voice or video) and wire-instruction fraud (0.4, 0.5).
requests.pass: Instructions confirmed verbally with a known officer at a number we obtained independently; beneficiary account title matches the deal entity.
requests.fail: Instructions received or changed only by message; account titled to someone other than the deal entity.
requests.verify: Our treasury performs the call-back.

requests.request: Officer's certificate bringing down every hints-log answer, the self-disclosure questionnaire and the beneficial-ownership certification as true at closing.
requests.format: Signed certificate.
requests.why: Fraud claims based on diligence statements can survive non-reliance clauses only if the statements are captured (0.16).
requests.pass: Certificate delivered without exceptions, or exceptions resolved before funding.
requests.fail: Exceptions or refusal to certify.
requests.verify: Counsel attaches the hints log to the certificate.

requests.request: Re-check at signing of every 0.18 regulatory status line the deal relies on (SEC Private Fund Adviser rules, IA AML rule, CTA BOI, CDD Rule, 506(c), OFAC, SEC crypto, GENIUS Act, cannabis scheduling, OBBBA credits, retail access, ILPA templates, NVCA documents, CRE workouts, SR 13-3, HUD sizing).
requests.format: Counsel memo dated at signing.
requests.why: Rules changed between 2024 and 2026 and keep changing (0.18).
requests.pass: Every relied-on line is current at signing.
requests.fail: Any line stale or misdescribed in the documents.
requests.verify: Counsel checks primary sources.

requests.request: 100-day compliance integration and audit plan for the target, with owners and dates.
requests.format: Written plan.
requests.why: DOJ asks whether acquirers integrate targets into controls promptly and audit them post-close (0.15).
requests.pass: Plan names owners, dates and audit scope, covering every gap in the compliance diligence.
requests.fail: No plan or gaps left unassigned.
requests.verify: Monitor completion at day 100.

requests.request: Closing funds-flow memorandum reconciled to the sources-and-uses table.
requests.format: Signed funds flow with wire details.
requests.why: Leakage to insiders at closing (0.4).
requests.pass: Funds flow ties to sources and uses to the dollar; every payee verified.
requests.fail: Unexplained payees or amounts.
requests.verify: Reconcile to bank statements after funding.

requests.request: Security documents, perfected filings and lien-release evidence for every asset securing our position, and intercreditor terms with all other secured parties.
requests.format: Filed UCC-1s, recorded mortgages, control agreements, payoff letters, intercreditor agreement.
requests.why: Every claim on the same asset must be visible and ranked (Spine).
requests.pass: Our security is perfected with the intended priority and all prior liens are released or subordinated.
requests.fail: Unperfected security or surviving prior liens.
requests.verify: Post-closing search confirms filings.

requests.request: Quarterly reporting package: financial statements, covenant compliance certificate, bank statements for every account, and average-versus-period-end balances of cash and debt.
requests.format: Delivered within the contractual deadline; bank statements delivered by the bank or portal.
requests.why: Frauds caught within 6 months had a median loss of $40,000 against $1.115M for those lasting over 5 years; monitoring frequency is a loss-control variable (0.4).
requests.pass: Package complete each quarter, cash reconciles to statements, period-end balances consistent with averages, covenants met.
requests.fail: Late or incomplete packages; reconciliation breaks; quarter-end window dressing.
requests.verify: Reconcile to bank data obtained directly.

requests.request: Annual audited financial statements by the named auditor, with the management letter.
requests.format: Auditor-signed statements and letter.
requests.why: An unaudited fund is an automatic pass; a late audit is an early warning (0.4, 0.15).
requests.pass: Unqualified opinion delivered on the contractual date; management-letter points remediated.
requests.fail: Late audit, qualification or auditor change.
requests.verify: Call the audit partner annually.

requests.request: Reconciliation of every distribution paid to its source account and to underlying asset or portfolio cash flow.
requests.format: Schedule per distribution with bank references.
requests.why: GPB Capital paid distributions from new capital (0.4).
requests.pass: Every distribution traces to operating cash flow.
requests.fail: Any distribution funded by new capital or undisclosed borrowing.
requests.verify: Trace in bank statements.

requests.request: Loan-level log of amend-and-extend actions, PIK toggles and maturity extensions, stating whether each was a documented workout.
requests.format: Quarterly log.
requests.why: Private lenders can forbear indefinitely; PIK share of BDC income has doubled since 2019 (0.10, 0.18).
requests.pass: Each modification is documented as a workout consistent with the 2023 Interagency Policy Statement on CRE workouts.
requests.fail: Serial extensions or PIK toggles without documentation; deferred loss recognition.
requests.verify: Review lender files and marks.

requests.request: Continuous sanctions screening of every party and annual KYC refresh, including changes in beneficial ownership.
requests.format: Vendor alerts and annual refreshed certifications.
requests.why: Sanctions screening must continue after onboarding (0.3).
requests.pass: No hits; ownership changes notified and screened.
requests.fail: Hit or unreported ownership change.
requests.verify: Vendor engaged by us.

requests.request: Prompt written notice of litigation, regulatory inquiries, key-person events, auditor changes, covenant breaches, restatements and hotline matters involving senior management.
requests.format: Contractual notice within the agreed period.
requests.why: Small irregularities escalate; white-collar misconduct runs about six years before exposure, usually surfacing in a downturn (0.2, 0.4).
requests.pass: Every event notified within the contractual period.
requests.fail: Events learned from third parties before the sponsor notified.
requests.verify: Cross-check dockets and regulator sites quarterly.

requests.request: Annual hotline statistics (volume, categories, resolution times) and internal investigations log update.
requests.format: Report.
requests.why: Tips detect 43% of frauds (0.15).
requests.pass: Hotline functioning with plausible volume and timely resolution.
requests.fail: Volume falls to zero or matters unresolved.
requests.verify: Retest the hotline annually.

requests.request: Annual insurance certificates, renewal terms and premium changes.
requests.format: Certificates from insurers or broker.
requests.why: Premium repricing mirrors climate risk (0.19).
requests.pass: Coverage maintained at required limits; premium within the 2x stress.
requests.fail: Lapse, non-renewal, or move to an insurer of last resort.
requests.verify: Broker confirms directly.

requests.request: Annual UCC, lien and judgment search refresh across the issuer, affiliates and principal-owned entities.
requests.format: Search reports dated within the reporting year, across the certified org chart's entities.
requests.why: New pledges can appear after closing (0.5).
requests.pass: No filing appears that is not on the updated claims schedule.
requests.fail: A new secured party, lien or judgment that the sponsor did not disclose.
requests.verify: Search firm engaged by us, using the debtor names from our own secretary-of-state pulls.

requests.request: Quarterly ILPA Reporting Template and an annual independent valuation of Level 3 positions.
requests.format: ILPA template; valuation report.
requests.why: Private marks lag public proxies by at least four quarters (0.6, 0.18).
requests.pass: Delivered on time; marks consistent with public proxies and independent valuation.
requests.fail: Missing reports; marks above public-implied values.
requests.verify: Compare to BDC Schedules of Investments and public indices.

requests.request: Quarterly redemption-queue, gate-usage and liquidity-coverage report.
requests.format: Administrator report.
requests.why: Semi-liquid vehicles face a leverage-redemption feedback loop (0.10, 0.11).
requests.pass: Liquidity coverage stays above the redemption cap.
requests.fail: Queues building or gates used.
requests.verify: Administrator delivers directly.

requests.request: Quarterly financing-line report: balances, haircuts, advance rates, margin calls and renewal dates.
requests.format: Lender statements.
requests.why: Advance rates are a state variable; lenders cut them when you need them (0.10).
requests.pass: No adverse change unaddressed; renewals scheduled.
requests.fail: Margin calls or non-renewal notices.
requests.verify: Lender statements delivered directly.

requests.request: Quarterly treasury map: balances by bank and insured share, pooled cash vehicles, and counterparty indicators.
requests.format: Schedule tied to statements.
requests.why: Where the cash sits and who can gate it changes over time (0.11).
requests.pass: Cash remains spread or insured; no new concentration.
requests.fail: Concentration in a single uninsured bank or gateable vehicle.
requests.verify: Confirm balances with banks.

requests.request: Post-mortem inputs at the date diarized at the vote and after any loss or surprise: actual versus underwriting for each key variable.
requests.format: Variance report.
requests.why: Post-mortems separate misjudged variables from bad luck (0.1, 0.12).
requests.pass: Delivered with full variance detail.
requests.fail: Refused or incomplete.
requests.verify: Our team runs the post-mortem.

kill_tests.test: One person decides on investments, moves cash and reports results, with no independent administrator, custodian or auditor separating those duties.
Sponsor refuses direct, unsolicited confirmation with any bank, administrator, auditor, custodian, prime broker, servicer or processor, or refuses on-site diligence.
Bank, custody or performance statements are available only as sponsor-produced copies and the sponsor will not authorize delivery from the institution.

No accounting function: no in-house CFO or controller, no employee census that reconciles to payroll, or customer assets and matching liabilities not recorded on the balance sheet (the bible calls this an automatic pass).
The fund or vehicle has never been audited (the bible calls an unaudited fund an automatic pass).

Any investor, beneficial owner, borrower or counterparty is on the OFAC SDN or sectoral lists, UN, EU or UK lists, or is owned 50% or more in aggregate by blocked persons; or a crypto address in the chain is sanctioned.
Beneficial owners (every 25% owner and a control person) cannot be identified and verified through our own CDD.
Source of funds or source of wealth for the sponsor's commitment or any principal cannot be established with third-party documents.
Distributions or returns to existing investors are funded by new investor money (the definition of a Ponzi), or a fixed or guaranteed above-market return cannot be traced to asset cash flow.
Independent background check finds a material criminal, fraud, securities or regulatory matter that the sponsor or a principal did not disclose in the signed self-disclosure.
Resume, licence, degree or claimed prior exit of a principal is shown to be fabricated or materially inflated.
Collateral is found pledged to another party, or item-level dedupe finds the same receivable, VIN or serial number in another lender's borrowing base.

An undisclosed lien, UCC filing, guarantee, factoring or supply-chain-finance facility is found on the issuer, an affiliate or a principal-owned entity and the sponsor cannot explain why it was omitted.
Valuations were prepared by the principal while the sponsor claimed an independent valuation expert or pricing service.
The manager can alter pricing inputs or choose models for an 'independent' pricing service and refuses an administrator price check on Level 3 positions.
A single person holds the keys to crypto assets, or no key-ceremony documentation and quorum test can be produced.
Customer or fund assets are commingled with personal or sponsor accounts, or used for other ventures.
Bank or administrator wire-approval matrix shows a single person can release funds, or contradicts the sponsor's description and the sponsor cannot reconcile it.
No bindable insurance is available for a real asset for the full hold period (insurability is a diligence gate).
A fund has neither key-person dissolution or suspension nor a workable removal right (the bible treats this as no governance).
Wire or principal instructions cannot be verified by call-back to an independently obtained number.
Named validators, partners, customers or co-investors deny the relationship or the diligence the sponsor attributed to them.
The sponsor refuses to provide 36 months of bank statements for every account, or the bank confirmations show accounts missing from the set provided.
Proof of reserves cannot be matched with proof of liabilities as of the same block for a custodian, exchange or crypto lender.
The sponsor's recent funds land consistently in the third or fourth quartile of a named, vintage-matched benchmark.

red_flags.flag: One person decides, moves cash and reports.
red_flags.check: Obtain the bank or administrator signatory list and wire matrix directly; map who decides, who moves cash and who reports.

red_flags.flag: Collusion risk: a long-tenured, closed inner circle controls both reporting and cash.
red_flags.check: Background-check the CFO, controller and wire releaser; interview staff below the principals; segregation is necessary, not sufficient.

red_flags.flag: No independent administrator, custodian or auditor, or an auditor too small for the mandate (two-partner firm, no peer review).
red_flags.check: Confirm auditor size, PCAOB registration and peer review; call the audit partner.

red_flags.flag: Non-Big 4 or undersized auditor combined with internal pricing.
red_flags.check: Require administrator or third-party pricing for a Level 3 sample; justify the auditor choice.

red_flags.flag: Returns smooth relative to the stated strategy, at any level.
red_flags.check: Compare volatility and drawdowns with the asset class; compute MPPM; treat low volatility and low correlation as an accounting artifact.

red_flags.flag: Guaranteed or fixed above-market returns; a fixed 'distribution rate' on an illiquid fund.
red_flags.check: Trace every distribution to its source account and to asset cash flow.

red_flags.flag: Refusal to allow on-site diligence or direct contact with the administrator, auditor, custodian or prime broker.
red_flags.check: Make direct contact a condition precedent.

red_flags.flag: Statements produced by the manager rather than an independent third party.
red_flags.check: Obtain statements directly from banks and custodians.

red_flags.flag: New-investor money paying old-investor returns.
red_flags.check: Proof of cash and distribution tracing.

red_flags.flag: Commingling of personal and fund accounts.
red_flags.check: Trace flows in 36 months of statements for every account the principals control.

red_flags.flag: No accounting function, no employee census, customer assets off the balance sheet.
red_flags.check: Confirm a controller or CFO, reconcile census to payroll, check customer assets and liabilities on the balance sheet.

red_flags.flag: Customer assets used for other ventures or held in sponsor-titled or omnibus accounts.
red_flags.check: Confirm accounts titled to the fund or customer at an independent custodian and reconciled to liabilities.

red_flags.flag: A single key holder (crypto); hot and cold wallets sharing keys.
red_flags.check: Key-ceremony documentation and witnessed quorum test.

red_flags.flag: Period-end balances that differ from intra-quarter averages; recurring financing that unwinds just after period-end.
red_flags.check: Request average daily or intra-quarter balances of cash, debt and assets.

red_flags.flag: Off-balance-sheet vehicles, guarantees, keepwells or 'moral obligation' support; factoring, supply-chain finance or receivables sales excluded from leverage.
red_flags.check: List all of them, require a consolidated look-through and add them to leverage.

red_flags.flag: Multiple warehouse, factoring or inventory-finance providers each seeing only their own collateral, and no single party that sees all of it.
red_flags.check: UCC sweep across all secured parties and affiliates; item-level dedupe by an independent collateral agent.

red_flags.flag: Classic sales-side tells: overselling, steering good deals to insiders, churning for fees, adjusted earnings with no GAAP reconciliation, pressure to act fast.
red_flags.check: Related-party schedule, fee schedule, GAAP reconciliation, written diligence floor.

red_flags.flag: 'X and Y are already in' offered as diligence.
red_flags.check: Ask what diligence those investors did and confirm with them directly.

red_flags.flag: Small, explained-away irregularities: a late audit, a restated quarter, an unbooked rebate.
red_flags.check: Track every irregularity as a finding in the hints log; ask the auditor directly.

red_flags.flag: Wire instructions or principal instructions received only by message (risk of synthetic voice or video).
red_flags.check: Call back on an independently obtained number.

red_flags.flag: Repeated optimistic forecast misses in the sponsor's or management's history.
red_flags.check: Compare every past projection with actuals.

red_flags.flag: Founder super-voting control without a sunset; board of celebrities with no domain experts.
red_flags.check: Map voting control, board seats and each director's domain expertise; price super-voting control.

red_flags.flag: Verbal numbers that differ from documents; refused or deflected questions.
red_flags.check: Write down every number given in meetings and reconcile to the data room; track refusals as a reported field.

red_flags.flag: Manager's description of cash controls differs from the administrator's.
red_flags.check: Obtain the wire matrix from the administrator.

red_flags.flag: Resume inflation by any principal.
red_flags.check: Verify employment, education and licences directly.

red_flags.flag: A 'CFO' who is really a controller; titles that do not match the job.
red_flags.check: Interview the finance team and review CVs.

red_flags.flag: Sponsor deal pace or AUM doubling without the operating bench.
red_flags.check: Chart deals per year and AUM against team size.

red_flags.flag: Seller-imposed deadline; competitive round used to cut the diligence floor.
red_flags.check: Set the diligence floor in writing; use cooling-off periods.

red_flags.flag: Lead investor or sponsor cannot state hours with management in person, sites visited and references called.
red_flags.check: Ask the lead directly and record diligence intensity.

red_flags.flag: 'Proprietary deal' no one can corroborate.
red_flags.check: Ask who else saw it and whether a banker ran a process.

red_flags.flag: Deal champion also runs the valuation.
red_flags.check: Separate deal champions from the valuation team; set the walk-away price before bidding.

red_flags.flag: Investment case resting on pitch delivery or founder charisma rather than data-room evidence.
red_flags.check: Score the written materials before the pitch with a fixed rubric and more than one rater.

red_flags.flag: Terms of art no one in the approval chain can restate in one sentence with a number.
red_flags.check: Jargon test and plain-language glossary annex.

red_flags.flag: Risk limits raised to fit positions; CRO replaced by a dealmaker.
red_flags.check: Request the limit-breach log and limit-change record for 24 months; ask who the CRO reports to.

red_flags.flag: Track record compounded, gross-only, cherry-picked, or attributed to people who have left.
red_flags.check: Recompute from LP cash flows; attribute deals to partners; show with and without the top 1 or 2 outcomes.

red_flags.flag: Track record presented as a compounded IRR or compared with a time-weighted index.
red_flags.check: Use PME or KS-PME; never compound an IRR.

red_flags.flag: Sharpe or Sortino offered as proof of skill for a strategy using options or leverage.
red_flags.check: Compute MPPM; benchmark against levered put-writing.

red_flags.flag: No ILPA Performance Template for prior funds.
red_flags.check: Request it for every prior fund; refusal is a signal.

red_flags.flag: 'Top quartile' without naming the benchmark, vintage and whether dead funds are included.
red_flags.check: Require the benchmark details; haircut unadjusted peer averages by several hundred bp.

red_flags.flag: Successor fund far larger than the funds that earned the record, without a matching increase in senior team.
red_flags.check: Compare fund size, team size and deals per partner.

red_flags.flag: Non-functional or discouraged whistleblower hotline.
red_flags.check: Call or e-mail the hotline; request 3 years of statistics.

red_flags.flag: Unaudited fund.
red_flags.check: Automatic pass; also test portfolio-company card and payroll spend.

red_flags.flag: Valuations prepared by the principal while an 'independent expert' is claimed.
red_flags.check: Obtain the valuation firm's engagement letter and call the firm.

red_flags.flag: Complex illiquid product sold to retail; heavy deployment pressure.
red_flags.check: Ask for the annual deployment target against the market; read gates.

red_flags.flag: Deck cites the round's price, a marquee co-investor or a national demand forecast as validation, in an asset class scoring late-cycle on three or more scorecard lines.
red_flags.check: Score the 0.10 cycle scorecard; name the exit buyer and multiple once supply arrives.

red_flags.flag: Single uninsured bank; cash in pooled vehicles that can gate.
red_flags.check: Bank account list with insured share; look through MMFs; model a 6-to-24-month gate.

red_flags.flag: Strategic investor with a financing veto.
red_flags.check: List every investor veto over financings and M&A.

red_flags.flag: Sponsor pivoting to retail or 401(k) capital.
red_flags.check: Treat as a cycle signal; read the vehicle's gates, valuation frequency and fee layers.

red_flags.flag: Stated-income pool whose income growth outruns local IRS income growth.
red_flags.check: Verify with IRS transcripts (4506-C) and benchmark against IRS SOI and BLS wages.

red_flags.flag: Supplier sales growth outrunning major customers' purchase growth; jumps in customers' inventory and payables (channel stuffing).
red_flags.check: Compare top-10 customer sales with each customer's purchases, inventory and AP.

red_flags.flag: Material unexplained changes in filing or management-letter language (risk factors, MD&A, legal proceedings).
red_flags.check: Diff the last 8 quarters and require an explanation for each edit.

red_flags.flag: Bunching of loans or a default jump at an eligibility cutoff (FICO, DTI).
red_flags.check: Plot the tape around every cutoff.

red_flags.flag: Leverage justified by what lenders will provide rather than cash-flow volatility; maximum permitted leverage far above closing leverage.
red_flags.check: Compute maximum permitted leverage under all baskets and add-backs.

red_flags.flag: Amend-and-extend, PIK toggles or serial maturity extensions without a documented workout.
red_flags.check: Track modifications by loan.

red_flags.flag: Default rate quoted without its definition.
red_flags.check: Ask which definition (covenant, payment, realized loss).

red_flags.flag: Margin expansion assumed from scale without a costed bridge.
red_flags.check: Hold margins flat in the base case.

red_flags.flag: Return depends on exit multiple above entry.
red_flags.check: Show exit = entry with margins flat, and entry minus 1 to 2 turns.

red_flags.flag: Pricing or marking off the headline post-money of a round with preferences, ratchets or participation.
red_flags.check: Value the specific security.

red_flags.flag: Growth that is a 'hockey stick made entirely of acquisition', with weakening cohorts.
red_flags.check: Track revenue from customers acquired in the period against prior cohorts.

red_flags.flag: Successor or co-invest offered while the main fund does not take its full pro rata.
red_flags.check: Ask why the GP is syndicating.

red_flags.flag: Early portfolio commentary dwelling on refinancing, covenants or capital structure.
red_flags.check: Read the commentary history, not just the marks.

red_flags.flag: Water rights carried as permanent assets with no impairment for junior priority.
red_flags.check: Confirm will-serve letter, source and seniority.

red_flags.flag: Asset coverage depends on a state insurer of last resort.
red_flags.check: Obtain bindable quotes for the full hold and stress a 2x premium.

red_flags.flag: Returns rely on a government lease ETO not being exercised, appropriations that can be swept, or tax credits that may be lost.
red_flags.check: Model ETO exercise at first date, sweep loss and a no-credit downside.

red_flags.flag: Draw commitment from a regional or bank-like lender that does not survive lender failure.
red_flags.check: Check the lender's funding mix and assignment or replacement rights.

red_flags.flag: Fund with neither key-person dissolution nor a workable removal right.
red_flags.check: Negotiate before signing; otherwise treat as no governance.

red_flags.flag: GP has no voluntary AML program and nobody runs KYC on the other LPs.
red_flags.check: Ask for the AML and sanctions policy and who performs investor KYC.

red_flags.flag: Major data vendor or administrator switched in the last 3 years without a clear reason.
red_flags.check: Ask why and call the former provider.

red_flags.flag: Absence of an SEC case cited as evidence of crypto compliance.
red_flags.check: Rely on custody, audit and on-chain verification.

red_flags.flag: Deck describes a regulatory status that is out of date (for example 'cannabis is now Schedule III' for adult-use).
red_flags.check: Check every 0.18 line at signing.

red_flags.flag: Insured buyers diligencing less because of R&W insurance.
red_flags.check: Remember RWI excludes known matters; diligence to the same floor.

red_flags.flag: Over-diversified roster masking low conviction; returns driven by financial engineering; momentum mistaken for skill; opacity about problems.
red_flags.check: Score the manager on the operating share of realized returns and on how openly it discusses problems.

red_flags.flag: DSCR computed on anticipated rather than in-place leases, or a cap rate built on cash flow rather than NOI.
red_flags.check: Recompute DSCR on in-place leases and confirm the cap-rate basis.

red_flags.flag: Thin diligence by the lead in a hot market (hours falling, competitive round).
red_flags.check: Hold our diligence floor regardless of competition; record intensity.
